### Part 3: Pipeline, Save-Time Bake, Sub-Selection, Multi-Instance & Preview Bugs

#### 21. `ConversionJobs.dispatchSave()` Drops All 9 Stage 7 Offline / Time / Duration Effects on Save (`BUG-02`)
* **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/ConversionJobs.java` (lines 572–589, 621–636)
* **Affected Effects**: `tempo`, `speedpitch`, `changepitch`, `slidestretch`, `paulstretch`, `fade`, `timeline`, `truncsil`, `generator`
* **Root Cause**:
  When `needsFxBake` is `true` at save time, `ConversionJobs.dispatchSave()` creates `DspChain chain = new DspChain(info.channels, cfg)` and calls `EditEngine.applyDspToRange(raw, 0, totalFrames, chain, null)`.
  * `EditEngine.applyDspToRange` only calls `chain.processInPlace(...)` -> `FxRackChain.processInPlace(...)`.
  * `FxRackChain.processInPlace()` (line 266) has `if (!p.isEnabled() || p.isOfflineOnly()) continue;`!
  * Unlike `StudioFragment.commitDspFx()`, `ConversionJobs.dispatchSave()` **never checks `chain.offlineProcessors()` and never calls `EditEngine.applyLengthChangingEffectToRange()`**!
* **Impact**: Any unbaked offline/time effect in the rack is **100% skipped and absent from the saved file**.

---

#### 22. `StudioFragment.runSaveDispatch()` + `resetFxRackAfterApply()` Destroys Sub-Selection FX Bakes and Re-Bakes Over the Full File (`BUG-03`)
* **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/StudioFragment.java` (lines 1104–1117, 1791–1797, 2497–2531)
* **Root Cause**:
  1. When the user selects a sub-range `[fxApplyTargetStart, fxApplyTargetEnd)` and commits FX (pressing Stop in FX mode), `commitDspFx()` bakes the effect into the sub-selection of `currentRawFile`, sets `dspBakedToRaw = true; dspSubRangeBaked = true;`, and calls `resetFxRackAfterApply()`.
  2. Despite the comment in `commitDspFx()` stating `"the raw file and waveform now carry the processed audio, so start a fresh, blank rack"`, `resetFxRackAfterApply()` **leaves all `dspConfig.slots` enabled (`dspConfig.isActive() == true`)**!
  3. If the user subsequently touches any FX knob (or toggles a slot), `onSlotMutated` sets `lastEditWasSubRangeBake = true; dspBakedToRaw = false;`.
  4. When the user saves (`runSaveDispatch()`, lines 1104–1117), it sees `lastEditWasSubRangeBake && dspConfig.isActive()`, **pops the undo stack** (discarding the sub-range bake!), marks `needsFxBake = true`, and passes `dspConfig` to `ConversionJobs.dispatchSave()`, which bakes the rack across **`[0, totalFrames)` (the entire recording)** instead of the user's sub-selection!

---

#### 23. `DspChain` Multi-Instance Legacy Stage Overwrite & `ProToneProcessor` Split vs. Unsplit Wet/Dry Mismatch (`BUG-22`)
* **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/DspChain.java` (lines 382–442, 672–778) and `ProToneProcessor.java` (lines 111–201)
* **Root Causes**:
  1. **Duplicate legacy stage primary `value` overwrite**:
     `Config.addOrFocusSlot()` appends duplicate `EffectSlot`s even for the 8 legacy stages. In `DspChain.ensureRackSlots()`, the first legacy slot binds to the canonical processor (`instanceKey == null`) and the second binds to a new instance (`instanceKey = "slot:..."`). However, `Config.syncLegacyFieldsFromSlots()` iterates over `slots` and overwrites `cfg.compPct` (and `noisePct`, `deEssPct`, `hpfCutoffHz`, `warmthPct`, `presencePct`, `gatePct`, `limiterPct`) with the **last** enabled slot's value! Then `rack.applyLegacyConfig(cfg)` writes that last slot's value into the **first** canonical processor (`instanceKey == null`), so both instances run with the 2nd slot's primary value!
  2. **`ProToneProcessor` (`Warmth` / `Presence`) wet/dry mix scales dB instead of linear sample mix**:
     `ProToneProcessor.handlesOwnWetDryMix()` returns `true` whenever `warmthSlotMix < 0.999f || presenceSlotMix < 0.999f`. Instead of mixing dry and wet audio linearly (`(1 - mix) * dry + mix * wet`), `updateTargets()` multiplies the shelf filter's **dB gain** by `wMix` and `pMix` (`9f * wMix` dB), producing a completely different frequency/phase response from linear wet/dry mixing (and differing from `processWarmthOnly` / `processPresenceOnly` when the two stages are separated in the rack!).

---

#### 24. `RawFloatPlayer` — Live Preview Playhead & Pause/Resume Broken on Time-Stretched Audio (`BUG-15`)
* **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/RawFloatPlayer.java` (lines 201–215, 302–342)
* **Root Cause**:
  When playing an offline-rendered buffer `offlineBuf` whose length `outFrames` differs from the source selection `limitFrame - startFramePos`:
  ```java
  public long positionFrames() {
      ...
      long head = track.getPlaybackHeadPosition() & 0xFFFFFFFFL;
      long limit = stopAtFrame > 0 ? stopAtFrame : totalFrames;
      return Math.min(limit, startFramePos + head);
  }
  ```
  `head` advances in **stretched output frames** (`0..outFrames`), whereas `limit` (`stopAtFrame`) is in **unstretched source frames** (`limitFrame`).
  * When an effect stretches audio longer (`outFrames > limitFrame - startFramePos`, e.g. `Change Tempo -50%`, `Paulstretch`, `Timeline Repeat`), `startFramePos + head` hits `limit` partway through playback: the UI playhead freezes at the end of the selection while audio keeps playing, and pressing **Pause** records `framePos = limitFrame`, losing the playback position!
  * When an effect shortens audio (`outFrames < limitFrame - startFramePos`, e.g. `Change Tempo +100%`, `Truncate Silence`), `startFramePos + head` stops short of `limitFrame` and jumps at playback completion.

---

#### 25. `EditEngine.applyLengthChangingEffectToRange` — Zero-Crossing Snap Drops/Duplicates Up to 240 Frames & Misreports `newTotal` (`BUG-16`)
* **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/EditEngine.java` (lines 460–517, 672–720)
* **Root Cause**:
  1. Line 470 reads the selected region `[startFrame, endFrame)` using the exact `endFrame`.
  2. Line 494 calls `saveTailFrom(raw, endFrame, tailTmp)`, which calls `Dsp.snapToZeroCrossing(..., endFrame, ..., 240)` and shifts the tail start by up to `±240 frames` (`±5 ms`), either duplicating or deleting up to 240 frames at `endFrame`!
  3. Line 502 calls `spliceTailAfterReplace(raw, startFrame + newFrames, tailTmp)`, which overlaps the first `fade` (`240`) frames of `tailTmp` over the last `240` frames of `rendered` (`replaceEndFrame - fade`), making the actual file length `startFrame + newFrames + tailFrames - fade`.
  4. Line 505 returns `long newTotal = startFrame + newFrames + tailFrames;` (off by `+fade` frames), which `StudioFragment.commitDspFx()` uses to compute `regionEnd` for the next offline processor in the chain!

---

#### 26. Double Wet/Dry Mixing (`BUG-30`) & `TeleValue` Keyboard Step Bypass / `FxPreviewPeaks` Flag (`BUG-31`)
* **Double Wet/Dry Mix (`BUG-30`)**:
  `FreeverbReverbProcessor` (`rv_wet`, `rv_dry`, `rv_wetonly`), `PhaserProcessor` (`ph_mix`), `ChorusFlangerProcessor` (`ch_mix`), and `VocoderProcessor` (`vc_orig`) each have internal dry/wet mix controls, while `handlesOwnWetDryMix()` returns `false` (default in `AudioProcessor`). Adjusting the rack slot's `Wet-Dry Mix` blends the dry input a second time on top of the already-mixed output.
* **`TeleValue.commitTyped()` Bypasses `FxParameter.step` (`BUG-31a`)**:
  In `TeleValue.java` (lines 483–505), double-tap keyboard entry parses `Double.parseDouble(raw) * valueScale` and calls `setValue(v, true)`, which clamps to `[min, max]` without rounding to `FxParameter.step` (`clampRaw`), allowing off-grid raw integer values.
* **`FxPreviewPeaks.renderRegionInternal()` Marks Non-Length-Changing Offline Effects as `lengthChanged = true` (`BUG-31b`)**:
  In `FxPreviewPeaks.java` (line 224), `isLiveTimeline` returns `new LiveRegionResult(..., true, newTotalFrames, ...)` unconditionally whenever `!chain.offlineProcessors().isEmpty()`, even for `FadeProcessor`, `ChangePitchProcessor`, and `TimelineUtilityProcessor` (Invert/Reverse) where `rFrames == dryFrames`.

---

## Prioritized Remediation Roadmap

1. **Immediate Data-Safety Fixes (P0)**:
   * **`EditEngine.flushTailIntoRange`**: Fix `raf.readFully(Dsp.toBytes(dry, ...))` by reading into a `byte[]` and converting via `Dsp.toFloats`, and mix decaying tail energy additively onto `dry` rather than overwriting post-selection audio with the full FX chain.
   * **`ConversionJobs.dispatchSave`**: Execute offline processors (`chain.offlineProcessors()` via `EditEngine.applyLengthChangingEffectToRange`) before `EditEngine.applyDspToRange` whenever `needsFxBake` is true.
   * **`StudioFragment.commitDspFx` / `resetFxRackAfterApply`**: Either clear/disable baked slots upon commit or persist the sub-selection range `[fxApplyTargetStart, fxApplyTargetEnd)` so save-time re-bakes never expand a sub-selection bake to `[0, totalFrames)`.
   * **`ClickRemovalProcessor` & `RepairProcessor`**: Remove the `!any` comb-filter branch in `ClickRemovalProcessor` and the `!repairedAny` fallback LPC branch in `RepairProcessor` so clean audio is never corrupted; fix `halfWin = Math.max(1, maxSpike / 2)` in `ClickRemovalProcessor`.
2. **Time & Envelope Semantics Fixes (P1)**:
   * **`BrickwallLimiterProcessor` & `ProLimiterProcessor`**: Remove `bufPeak * 0.72f` / `bufMax * 0.65f` adaptive thresholds so limiters only act near `Ceiling`; read the `peakRing` lookahead buffer; hold `gainDb` constant while `holdCounter > 0`; remove `ballisticsTrimDb` and `0.65f` input-gain scaling.
   * **`AutoDuckProcessor`**: Remove `Math.min(pauseFrames, frames / 2)` clamping on `pauseHoldLimit`, remove the fake LFO cycle when `(maxBlockDb - minBlockDb) <= 6f`, release `target` to `0.0 dB` after `pauseFrames`, and respect `duck_thresh` directly.
   * **`TruncateSilenceProcessor`**: Compute `keep = Math.max(1, Math.round(spanLen * (compressTo.getCurrentRaw() / 100f)))` in `"Compress Excess Silence"` mode.
   * **`VocoderProcessor`**: Convert `vc_release` from milliseconds to a sample-rate-aware coefficient: `float relCoef = 1f - (float) Math.exp(-1.0 / Math.max(1.0, release.getCurrentRaw() * 0.001 * sampleRate));`.
   * **`EchoProcessor` & `MultiDelayProcessor`**: Compute `getTailFrames()` dynamically from `echo_time`/`echo_decay` and `md_time * md_echoes`; use expanding tap offsets in `Reverse Bouncing Ball`; clamp `writePos` and resize `delayLine` cleanly.
   * **`FreeverbReverbProcessor`**: Scale `COMB_TUNING`, `ALLPASS_TUNING`, and `STEREO_SPREAD` by `sampleRate / 44100.0`; clamp/reset `prePos` when `preFrames` changes or `reset()` is called.
3. **Parameter Accuracy & Pipeline Polish (P2)**:
   * Fix `FadeProcessor` `Start Gain`/`End Gain` inversion on Fade Out and pre-warm `closingLp`.
   * Fix `AudioGeneratorTool` DTMF keypad mapping (`1209/1336/1477/1633 Hz` x `697/770/852/941 Hz`), noise waveform enum labels, and selection-length handling for `Silence`.
   * Fix `AmplifyProcessor.computeEffectiveGainDb`, `ClipFixProcessor` `refPeak`, `NoiseGateExpanderProcessor` `effThresh`, `WahwahProcessor.isAudible()`, `BassAndTrebleProcessor` `link` at `0 dB`, and `LoudnessNormalizationProcessor` early return before `loud_ceiling`.
   * Scale `RawFloatPlayer.positionFrames()` by `(double) (limitFrame - startFramePos) / outFrames` during offline buffer playback so the playhead tracks time-stretched audio accurately.

TAKEONE — VERIFICATION BUG REPORT
Source: exhaustive FX verification harness (see tools/fxverify/README.md)
Run at HEAD 5f6c767 on branch verify/fx-matrix; fixes for the product bugs are

SECTION 1 — PRODUCT BUGS (audio engine)
================================================================================

BUG 1 — Chorus diverges into non-finite samples at high feedback        [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : ChorusFlangerProcessor.processInPlace
Symptom   : At ch_fb = +90 % and -90 % the render becomes NaN/Inf. The DSP
            matrix counted 491,941 and 529,967 non-finite samples (of 576,000).
Root cause: Two feedback paths compound. The recursive state is one pole at
            fb (s[n] = delayed + fb*s[n-1]) and the ring writes back half the
            wet signal (ring = in + 0.5*fb*s[n]). Combined loop gain is
            0.5*fb*(1 + fb/(1-fb)), which exceeds 1 for fb > 2/3.
Fix       : Clamp the feedback coefficient to +-0.6 (loop gain 0.75 with
            margin) and recover a poisoned state instead of propagating it.
            Ring writes are also sanitized.
Before    : peak = non-finite (NaN), nonFinite = 491,941 / 529,967
After     : fb=+90 -> peak 1.93, nonFinite 0; fb=-90 -> peak 0.26, nonFinite 0
Bench     : 1 kHz tone 0.3, 12 s, 48 kHz, mono.

BUG 2 — Multi-Echo Delay feedback diverges (peak 5.76e11)                [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : MultiDelayProcessor.processInPlace
Symptom   : md_level = +1 dB (its own max) with md_echoes = 30 produced a peak
            of 5.762e+11 on an impulse train — the repeats compound without
            bound.
Root cause: The delay line is the feedback path and the loop gain equals the
            sum of tap amplitudes (pow(levelLin, k)). Above 0 dB that sum
            exceeds unity and grows with the number of echoes.
Fix       : Keep the audible taps as requested, but attenuate the signal
            written back into the delay line so the loop gain stays at 0.9
            (ampSum > 0.9 -> scale 0.9/ampSum), and sanitize the stored samples.
Before    : peak = 5.762e+11
After     : peak = 0.935, nonFinite = 0
Bench     : impulses at 0.5 s / 3.5 s / ... , 12 s, 30 echoes, +1 dB.

BUG 3 — Multi-Echo Delay wet sum exceeds full scale at +1 dB             [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : MultiDelayProcessor (tap summation)
Symptom   : Even with the loop stabilised, 30 taps at +1 dB sum to roughly
            +50 dB, so the wet signal alone exceeds full scale by >25 dB.
Root cause: The tap amplitudes are used as an unnormalised sum.
Fix       : Normalise the wet sum to unity when ampSum > 1 (decay shape kept).
            Defaults (level -6 dB, 5 echoes, ampSum ~0.97) are unchanged.
Before    : peak 26.7 (bounded but far above 0 dBFS)
After     : peak 0.93 with dry; taps keep their requested relative levels.

BUG 4 — Upward expansion boosts quiet material by the full ratio         [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : CompressorProcessor (dyncomp_upward = true)
Symptom   : "Upward (Expand)" produced a peak of 2856 on a gaps probe: quiet
            material below the threshold was amplified by up to +40 dB.
Root cause: The gain sign was inverted for the expand path
            (targetGain = -slope * over, with over negative -> positive gain).
Fix       : targetGain = max(-60 dB, slope * over) so below-threshold material
            is attenuated, as expansion means.

BUG 5 — Auto make-up gain cancels upward expansion                      [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : CompressorProcessor auto make-up
Symptom   : With dyncomp_makeup at its default (on), upward mode's attenuation
            was treated as "gain reduction" and compensated by up to +24 dB,
            boosting quiet passages back (residual peak 2.14 while the input
            peak was 0.30).
Root cause: Make-up gain is meaningful only for downward compression.
Fix       : Make-up is forced to 0 dB while upward mode is active.
After     : upward tone (-6 dB threshold, 20:1) -> out RMS 0.096 vs in 0.212,
            peak 0.136; gaps probe peak 0.136 (was 2.14/2856).

BUG 6 — Any diverging processor could poison the file with NaNs         [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : FxRackChain.processInPlace (defence in depth)
Symptom   : A single NaN from any stage survives every later effect and reaches
            the preview, the bake and the encoder; the safety ceiling only runs
            when the legacy limiter is armed.
Fix       : After each processor's pass, non-finite samples in the buffer are
            replaced with silence. Finite audio is untouched bit-for-bit.

Regression test for bugs 1-5: app/src/test/java/com/example/hello/
FxDivergenceGuardTest.java (3 tests, renders each case to completion, asserts
finite and bounded output). Verified locally against the compiled classes and in
CI unit shards.

Measurements (before -> after), all with nonFinite = 0 afterwards:
  chorus +90 %           ~492k NaN/Inf -> peak 1.93
  chorus -90 %           ~530k NaN/Inf -> peak 0.26
  multidelay +1 dB/30x   peak 5.762e11 -> peak 0.935
  dyncomp upward         peak 2856     -> peak 0.136


SECTION 2 — OPEN PRODUCT QUESTIONS (not changed; needs a decision)
================================================================================

OPEN 1 — Multi-Echo Delay is loud at its defaults
     With default settings (level -6 dB, 5 echoes, feedback loop gain ~0.97)
     the wet signal rings up to ~2.24 peak from a 0.3 input, i.e. above 0 dBFS.
     This predates the fixes above and was left alone because changing it
     redesigns the effect's level structure. Options: cap the loop gain at 0.8
     for all levels, or scale output to the dry level.

OPEN 2 — De-Esser Pro (legacy stage) parameters did not reach the DSP when the
     rack was built programmatically. The app's own UI path is unaffected: the
     card's onSlotMutated calls cfg.syncLegacyFieldsFromSlots() before saving.
     The verification harness now does the same, but the fix has not yet been
     re-run through the device tier.

OPEN 3 — Filter Curve EQ (fcurve) exposes 61 of its 67 parameters only by
     dragging the curve canvas; only out/npts/taps are shown as pill controls.
     Parameters pf0..pf31, pg0..pg31 and npts are therefore unreachable from
     the advanced grid. This is a UI design gap, not a DSP fault.

OPEN 4 — AMR-NB container quality: decoded band error 14.9 dB (bands <= 3.5 kHz)
     against the 48 kHz source. Expected for a 12.2 kbps narrow-band codec, but
     worth stating in the app's own docs/limits.


SECTION 3 — HARNESS / OBSERVABILITY ISSUES (fixed in the harness, not product)
================================================================================

H1 — Three device shards hang their instrumentation (stereoimg, plosive,
     slidestretch): attempt output is empty and each attempt burns its full
     20 minute host timeout; the job is then cancelled at the 60 minute ceiling.
     Mitigation: the per-parameter test now has a 38 minute internal budget and
     writes partial results instead of hanging. Root cause still unknown.
H2 — Apply was declared failed while an offline render (WSOLA pitch/tempo) was
     still running: a 0.5 s wait was used for a multi-second render. Fixed with
     a latch that waits for the work (up to 120 s) and records the failure text.
H3 — WAV readers read bitsPerSample at the wrong buffer offset (byteRate's
     position) and rejected every fixture as "not a 32-bit float WAV". Fixed
     with absolute offsets; also accepts WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE float output
     from the runner's ffmpeg.
H4 — Emulator script lines run in separate shells, so shell variables did not
     survive between lines. Fixed by resolving paths per line.
H5 — The Add-Effect dialog could not be driven reliably (soft keyboard covered
     the filtered row); the rack is now cleared and populated through the same
     production config path, and every parameter's control is still driven in
     the expanded pill. Marked `addedThroughUi=false` in each result.
H6 — The screen recording froze behind a "Pixel Launcher isn't responding"
     dialog, so every screenshot was the same frame. Fixed by hiding system
     error dialogs and stopping the launcher in the device jobs.
H7 — Analyzer: an unchanged render was judged as "expectation not met"; anchor
     metric names missed the cmp. prefix; probe-derived series metrics were
     unreadable; anchors were matched across effects. All fixed; a self-test
     (tools/fxverify/selftest.py) now proves the analyzer can fail.
H8 — Renderers wrote >200 GB of intermediate WAVs per full matrix; compact mode
     keeps metrics plus failing renders only.

TAKEONE STUDIO — DEEP AUDIT, BUG FIXES & FEATURE IMPLEMENTATION REPORT
========================================================================================

SUMMARY OF CHANGES
------------------
1. Default FX Preset Enabled on First Opening (`DspChain.java`, `StudioFragment.java`):
   - In `DspChain.Config.load(Context)`, when no saved slot configuration exists yet, the 4 starter slots (`NOISE_SUPPRESSION`, `DE_ESSER`, `COMPRESSOR`, `LOW_CUT_HPF`) are now seeded with `enabled = true`, `activePresetId` is set to `Preset.VOICE_POLISH.id`, and legacy fields are synced via `syncLegacyFieldsFromSlots()`.
   - In `StudioFragment`, added `fxEverOpened` tracking so opening the FX panel immediately arms the active default preset for live preview and bake on Save, while untouched dry recordings continue to use fast-path `StreamingEncoder` adoption.

2. Disabled Undo Popup (`StudioFragment.java`):
   - Removed `OptionsSheet.showTopPopup(requireContext(), "Edit undone");` from `StudioFragment.performStudioUndo()` and kept `performStudioRedo()` silent.

3. Robust 10-Step Undo & 10-Step Redo (`EditEngine.java`, `WaveformView.java`, `StudioFragment.java`, `fragment_studio.xml`, `ic_edit_redo.xml`):
   - Increased `EditEngine.MAX_UNDO_STEPS` from 3 to 10.
   - Added a bounded 10-step `redoStack` to `EditEngine.UndoJournal` (`canRedo()`, `redo(File)`, `undoDepth()`, `redoDepth()`, `clearRedo()`) that automatically clears when a new edit snapshot is recorded.
   - Upgraded `WaveformView` with 10-step `undoPeakStack`/`undoFramesPerBar` and `redoPeakStack`/`redoFramesPerBar` deques (`popUndoPeaks()`, `popRedoPeaks()`, `discardTopUndoPeaks()`), fixing an unbounded memory leak on `undoFramesPerBar`.
   - Added `ic_edit_redo.xml` and `@+id/btnEditRedo` to both portrait and landscape `fragment_studio.xml` layouts and wired `performStudioRedo()` and button state styling in `StudioFragment`.

4. Small Centered Popups with Large Rounded Corners (`bg_modal.xml`, `dialog_result.xml`, `OptionsSheet.java`, `TeleDialogs.java`, `StudioFragment.java`):
   - Increased `@drawable/bg_modal` corner radius from `22dp` to `28dp`.
   - Updated `layout/dialog_result.xml` from `match_parent` width to a compact `wrap_content` pill layout with `240dp` max text width.
   - Updated `OptionsSheet.styleAsTopPopup(Dialog)` to use `WRAP_CONTENT` width and height with `Gravity.CENTER` instead of stretching across `dm.widthPixels - dp(ctx, 24)` at the top of the screen.
   - Tightened centered modal width caps in `OptionsSheet.styleAsCenteredWithMaxWidth`, `TeleDialogs.style`, and `StudioFragment.showEffectDetailModal`.

5. Deep File-by-File Audit Fixes (Bugs, Edge Cases & Dead Code):
   - `app/src/main/res/mipmap/ic_launcher_round.xml`: Removed trailing non-XML plain text after `</layer-list>` that broke XML parsing.
   - `app/src/main/res/layout-land/fragment_studio.xml`: Replaced dead, unwired `fxPreviewBtn`/`fxApplyBtn` buttons in the landscape FX panel with `@+id/fxHint` matching portrait.
   - `MultibandCompressorProcessor.java`: Replaced independent LP/HP subtraction (`mid = buf - low - high`) with a complementary cascade split (`midHigh = buf - low`, `mid = midHigh - high`) to eliminate IIR phase-cancellation notches.
   - `DeEsserProcessor.java`: Removed `splitHigh` and computed the complementary high band as `buf[idx + c] - lowBand[f * ch + c]` to eliminate the 180° phase-cancellation notch at the crossover frequency.
   - `ClipFixProcessor.java`: Clamped `start - 3` and `end + 1` slope indices (`Math.max(0, start - 3)`, `Math.min(frames - 1, end + 1)`) to prevent `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` when clipping starts at frame 1 or 2.
   - `StereoImagingProcessor.java`: Promoted mono Haas delay buffer (`haasHist`, `haasPos`) to persistent instance fields reset in `reset()`, and removed the duplicate `/ 100f` division on `centerPct` that made stereo Center Isolation 100x too weak.
   - `VocoderProcessor.java`: Moved filter `setSections(...)` initialization from `processInPlace()` into `rebuild()` so filter states are not wiped at every block boundary.
   - `TruncateSilenceProcessor.java`: Removed unused `ByteArrayOutputStream` allocation and redundant byte-buffer conversions, copying `float[]` slices directly.
   - `DspChain.java` & `RawFloatPlayer.java`: Fixed `reset()` / `prepareOffline()` call order so two-pass processors (`Normalize`, `LoudnessNormalization`, `Amplify`) keep their scanned state; scaled offline tail samples by `mix`; guarded `if (!stop) framePos = limitFrame;` on offline preview pause; removed dead `isLegacyProcessor`.
   - `FormatConverter.java`, `FadeProcessor.java`, `StftProcessor.java`: Added `if (pct != lastPct)` progress throttling across all encoders in `FormatConverter` and removed unused fields (`lastCbAt`, `regionFrames`, `frameCounter`, `mag`, `phase`).

FILE 1/25: app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/DspChain.java
TITLE: Enable Default FX Preset (Voice Polish) on First Open, Fix Offline Region Render & Remove Dead Code
========================================================================================
EXPLANATION OF CHANGES:
1. Default FX Preset Enabled on First Open (`Config.load(Context)`):
   - Previously, when `dsp_slots_json` was absent on first install/launch, `Config.load()` defaulted `activePresetId` to `Preset.CLEAR_ALL.id` and seeded the 4 starter slots (`NOISE_SUPPRESSION`, `DE_ESSER`, `COMPRESSOR`, `LOW_CUT_HPF`) with `enabled = false`.
   - Changed the default `activePresetId` when `slotsJson == null` to `Preset.VOICE_POLISH.id`, seeded all 4 starter slots with `enabled = true`, and called `c.syncLegacyFieldsFromSlots()` so the FX rack opens with all 4 default effects enabled (`Effects Rack · 4 on`, `Preset: Voice Polish ▾`).
   - Preserved `new DspChain.Config()` (the no-arg constructor) as inactive so unit tests expecting an empty default constructor continue to pass.

2. Offline + In-Place Region Rendering Fixes (`renderRegionOfflineAndInPlace`):
   - Previously, `prepareOffline(...)` was called BEFORE `reset()`, which immediately wiped the two-pass analysis state (`scanned = false`) on `NormalizeProcessor`, `LoudnessNormalizationProcessor`, and `AmplifyProcessor`. Swapped the order so `reset()` runs before `prepareOffline(...)`.
   - When an offline processor lengthened a region (`next.length > buf.length`) with a partial wet/dry mix (`mix < 0.999f`), samples beyond `common = Math.min(buf.length, next.length)` were left unscaled at 100% wet instead of `next[i] *= mix`. Added tail scaling for `[common, next.length)`.
   - Replaced the manual per-processor loop over `rack.processors()` with `rack.processInPlace(block, n)` so automatic safety limiting and shared tone slot mix rules are respected.

3. Dead Code Removal:
   - Removed the unused private helper `isLegacyProcessor(AudioProcessor)`.

   - Updated `undo(File raw)` to snapshot the current pre-undo `raw` file into a `.redo` file on `redoStack` (bounded to 10 steps) before restoring the `.undo` snapshot.
   - Implemented `redo(File raw)` to snapshot the current `raw` file onto the undo `stack` (bounded to 10 steps) before restoring the `.redo` snapshot.

FILE 3/25: app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/WaveformView.java
TITLE: 10-Step Waveform Peak Undo/Redo, Memory Leak Fix & Aborted Edit Rollback
========================================================================================
EXPLANATION OF CHANGES:
1. Added 10-Step Waveform Peak Redo & Fixed `undoFramesPerBar` Leak:
   - Added `redoPeakStack` and `redoFramesPerBar` deques alongside `undoPeakStack` and `undoFramesPerBar`.
   - Updated `recordUndoPeaks()` to bound both `undoPeakStack` and `undoFramesPerBar` to `EditEngine.MAX_UNDO_STEPS` (10) — fixing a leak where `undoFramesPerBar` was never trimmed when `undoPeakStack` overflowed — and to clear `redoPeakStack` and `redoFramesPerBar` on every new edit.
   - Updated `popUndoPeaks()` to push the current waveform peaks and `framesPerBar` onto `redoPeakStack` / `redoFramesPerBar` (bounded to 10 steps) before restoring the undo snapshot.
   - Added `popRedoPeaks()` to restore the most recent redo peak snapshot and push the current state back onto `undoPeakStack` / `undoFramesPerBar`.
   - Added `discardTopUndoPeaks()` so that if an edit or FX commit fails before modifying the waveform, the pre-pushed undo snapshot can be discarded without polluting `redoPeakStack`.

FILE 13/25: app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/MultibandCompressorProcessor.java
TITLE: Fix 3-Band Crossover Phase Cancellation Bug
========================================================================================
EXPLANATION OF CHANGES:
1. Complementary Cascade Crossover Split:
   - Previously, `low` and `high` were filtered independently from `buf` using 4th-order Butterworth IIR filters and subtracted from `buf` (`mid[i] = buf[i] - low[i] - high[i]`). Because 4th-order IIR filters introduce a 360° phase rotation around their cutoff frequencies, subtracting `low` and `high` from the zero-phase dry `buf` created a faulty `mid` band that did not complement the phase-shifted `low` and `high` bands when band gains/compressors differed.
   - Replaced with a complementary cascade split (`midHigh[i] = buf[i] - low[i]`, then filter `midHigh` through `highPass` to obtain `high`, and `mid[i] = midHigh[i] - high[i]`), guaranteeing `low + mid + high == buf` to within floating-point precision (`< 1e-7`).
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UNIFIED DIFF:
--- a/app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/MultibandCompressorProcessor.java
+++ b/app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/MultibandCompressorProcessor.java
@@ -140,13 +140,15 @@

+        float[] midHigh = new float[frames * ch];
         float[] high = new float[frames * ch];
         float[] mid = new float[frames * ch];

         lowPass.process(low, frames, ch);
-        System.arraycopy(buf, 0, high, 0, high.length);

FILE 14/25: app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/DeEsserProcessor.java
TITLE: Fix Split-Band Crossover Notch Bug
========================================================================================
EXPLANATION OF CHANGES:
1. Complementary High-Band Extraction:
   - Previously, `DeEsserProcessor` used a 2nd-order Butterworth low-pass (`splitLow`) and a 2nd-order Butterworth high-pass (`splitHigh`) at the same frequency and summed `lowBand + highBand * g`. Because 2nd-order Butterworth LP and HP outputs are 180° out of phase at the crossover frequency, summing them at `g = 1.0` (0 dB reduction) cancelled the signal at the crossover frequency!
   - Removed `splitHigh` and computed the high band complementarily as `float high = buf[idx + c] - low;`, eliminating the crossover notch completely.

FILE: Takeone Conversion Pipeline Fixes.txt
=================================================================================
================================================================================
TAKEONE AUDIO CONVERSION PIPELINE FIXES & DEFAULT MUSIC FORMAT UPDATE (WAV 32-BIT)
================================================================================

SUMMARY OF CHANGES:
1. Default Music Recording Format Changed from FLAC to WAV 32-bit (WAV32):
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/SaveFormat.java
     SaveFormat.AUTO.effective(RecordPreset) now resolves to SaveFormat.WAV32
     whenever preset.autoSavesLossless is true (RecordPreset.MUSIC).
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/RecordPreset.java
     Updated Javadoc for autoSavesLossless to document WAV 32-bit float.
   - app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
     Updated preset_music_sub subtitle from '(FLAC)' to '(WAV 32-bit)'.
   - Updated SaveFormatTest.java and EncodeFormatsTest.java expectations.

2. Fixed Replace-While-Converting Bug in Conversion Pipeline:
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/ConversionJobs.java
     * Registers NEG_TO_RAW immediately inside enqueue() and sweep() so in-flight
       and recently-completed jobs are always resolvable by negative takeId even
       before LibraryFragment.convertingCards() refreshes.
     * Sets job.title to replaceTitle when enqueueing a replacement conversion.
     * In dispatchSave(): immediately cancels any active conversion via
       cancelForReplace(ctx, replaceTakeId) (deleting its .raw.wav, .part, and
       .conv.json sidecar), and if replaceTakeId > 0 (either replacing an
       existing take or a conversion that finished while the user was editing
       in Studio), immediately calls TakesRepository.deleteImmediateForReplace()
       before starting the new conversion and resets replaceTakeId = -1L.
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/TakesRepository.java
     * Added deleteImmediateForReplace(long targetId) to immediately remove the
       previous Take entry from memory/Room and hard-delete its backing audio
       file on disk before the new conversion starts.
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/FormatConverter.java
     * Removed the 250ms / pct != lastPct callback throttling in toWav16,
       toWav24, toWav32, encodeMuxed (toM4a/toOpus), and toFlac so progress
       callbacks fire on every chunk (~16k-64k frames), allowing
       ConversionService to abort a cancelled conversion immediately within
       milliseconds and free WORKER_SERIAL_LOCK for the new conversion.
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/ConversionService.java
     * Checks job.cancelled on every chunk callback while deduplicating UI/notif
       updates to percentage changes (pct != lastReportedPct[0]).
   - app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/StudioFragment.java & RecordingService.java
     * Updated inline-adoption callbacks after dispatchSave() to use replaceTitle
       directly since dispatchSave() has already deleted the replaced file.
   - app/src/test/java/com/example/hello/ConversionJobsTest.java
     * Added unit test verifying immediate cancellation/deletion on replace.

package com.example.hello;

import android.content.Context;
import android.media.MediaCodecInfo;
import android.media.MediaCodecList;
import android.media.MediaFormat;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Container/codec the user wants the finished take written in.
 *
 * &lt;p&gt;Audio is always captured to a crash-safe 32-bit float WAV on disk first;
 * this choice only governs the final conversion step after the user stops.
 *
 * &lt;p&gt;WAV16/WAV24/WAV32 are written by our own pure-Java writer (always available);
 * M4A uses the baseline AAC encoder mandated by the Android CDD. The other
 * formats (FLAC, Opus, AMR-NB, AMR-WB) are gated by a one-shot
 * {@link MediaCodecList} probe so the picker never offers an encoder the
 * device does not actually have.
 */
public enum SaveFormat {
    AUTO("auto", R.string.save_auto, R.string.save_auto_sub, "AUTO"),
    M4A("m4a", R.string.save_m4a, R.string.save_m4a_sub, "M4A"),
    WAV16("wav16", R.string.save_wav16, R.string.save_wav16_sub, "WAV"),
    WAV24("wav24", R.string.save_wav24, R.string.save_wav24_sub, "WAV24"),
    WAV32("wav32", R.string.save_wav32, R.string.save_wav32_sub, "WAV32"),
    FLAC("flac", R.string.save_flac, R.string.save_flac_sub, "FLAC"),
    OPUS("opus", R.string.save_opus, R.string.save_opus_sub, "OPUS"),
    AMR_NB("amr_nb", R.string.save_amr_nb, R.string.save_amr_nb_sub, "AMR"),
    AMR_WB("amr_wb", R.string.save_amr_wb, R.string.save_amr_wb_sub, "AMR-WB");

    public final String id;
    public final int titleRes;
    public final int subRes;
    /** Short badge stored on the library card ("M4A", "WAV", "FLAC", …). */
    public final String badge;

    private static final String PREFS = "takeone";
    private static final String KEY = "save_format";
    private static volatile SaveFormat cached;
    private static final Map<SaveFormat, Boolean> AVAIL = new HashMap<>();

    SaveFormat(String id, int titleRes, int subRes, String badge) {
        this.id = id;
        this.titleRes = titleRes;
        this.subRes = subRes;
        this.badge = badge;
    }

    public static SaveFormat of(String id) {
        if (id != null) {
            for (SaveFormat f : values()) {
                if (f.id.equalsIgnoreCase(id)) return f;
            }
        }
        return AUTO;
    }

    public static SaveFormat load(Context ctx) {
        SaveFormat c = cached;
        if (c != null) return c;
        try {
            String raw = ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                    .getString(KEY, AUTO.id);
            c = of(raw);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            c = AUTO;
        }
        cached = c;
        return c;
    }

    public void save(Context ctx) {
        cached = this;
        try {
            ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                    .edit().putString(KEY, id).apply();
        } catch (Exception ignored) {}
    }

    /** True if this device can actually encode this format right now. */
    public synchronized boolean available(Context ctx) {
        switch (this) {
            case AUTO:
            case M4A:
            case WAV16:
            case WAV24:
            case WAV32:
                return true;
            case OPUS:
                // MediaMuxer only gained OGG/WEBM Opus support across the
                // board on API 29; older builds have the codec but no muxer.
                if (android.os.Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < 26) return false;
                break;
            case FLAC:
            case AMR_NB:
            case AMR_WB:
                break;
        }
        Boolean hit = AVAIL.get(this);
        if (hit != null) return hit;
        boolean ok = hasEncoder(encoderMime());
        AVAIL.put(this, ok);
        return ok;
    }

    /**
     * Proves the device can actually instantiate and configure the encoder
     * at our recording geometry — not merely that it lists the MIME in
     * {@link MediaCodecList}. Some builds advertise a codec that then throws
     * on {@code configure()} for 48 kHz stereo.
     */
    private boolean hasEncoder(String mime) {
        if (mime == null) return true;
        try {
            MediaCodecList list = new MediaCodecList(MediaCodecList.ALL_CODECS);
            boolean listed = false;
            for (MediaCodecInfo info : list.getCodecInfos()) {
                if (!info.isEncoder()) continue;
                for (String t : info.getSupportedTypes()) {
                    if (mime.equalsIgnoreCase(t)) {
                        listed = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (listed) break;
            }
            if (!listed) return false;
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    public String encoderMime() {
        switch (this) {
            case M4A: return MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_AUDIO_AAC;
            case FLAC: return "audio/flac";
            case OPUS: return "audio/opus";
            case AMR_NB: return "audio/3gpp";
            case AMR_WB: return "audio/amr-wb";
            default: return null;
        }
    }

    /** File extension (without dot) for a resolved format. */
    public String extension() {
        switch (this) {
            case WAV16:
            case WAV24:
            case WAV32: return "wav";
            case AMR_NB:
            case AMR_WB: return "3gp";
            case FLAC: return "flac";
            case OPUS:
                return android.os.Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 29 ? "opus" : "webm";
            case M4A:
            case AUTO:
            default: return "m4a";
        }
    }

    /**
     * Resolves {@link #AUTO} against the active preset:
     * &lt;ul&gt;
     *   &lt;li&gt;Voice Memo / Podcast — speech, where AAC is transparent at a
     *       tenth of the size, so Auto picks {@link #M4A}.</li>
     *   &lt;li&gt;Music — unprocessed stereo master where any lossy pass
     *       discards real detail, so Auto saves lossless 32-bit float WAV
     *       ({@link #WAV32}).</li>
     * &lt;/ul&gt;
     * Any explicit choice is returned unchanged.
     */
    public SaveFormat effective(RecordPreset preset) {
        if (this != AUTO) return this;
        if (preset != null && preset.autoSavesLossless) {
            return WAV32;
        }
        return M4A;
    }

    /**
     * Next format to switch to when an encoder for {@code this} crashes the
     * process mid-save. Walks down to a simpler encoder and finally to
     * {@link #WAV16}, which is our own pure-Java writer (no MediaCodec) and
     * cannot die natively. Null when already at the bottom. FLAC falls back
     * to WAV24, never to lossy AAC: a lossless save must not silently
     * degrade when pure-Java WAV24 is available.
     */
    public SaveFormat fallbackAfterCrash() {
        switch (this) {
            case OPUS:
            case AMR_NB:
            case AMR_WB:
                return M4A;
            case FLAC:
                return WAV24;
            case M4A:
            case AUTO:
                return WAV16;
            case WAV16:
            case WAV24:
            case WAV32:
            default:
                return null;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Approximate bytes written per minute of audio when saved in this
     * format under the given preset. Constant-rate estimates are exact;
     * FLAC is a content-dependent guess (see {@link #FLAC_RATIO}).
     */
    public long bytesPerMinute(RecordPreset preset) {
        SaveFormat eff = effective(preset);
        int ch = preset != null ? Math.max(1, preset.channels) : 2;
        int br = preset != null ? preset.aacBitrate : 128000;
        long sr = RecordingEngine.SAMPLE_RATE;
        switch (eff) {
            case WAV16:
                return sr * ch * 2 * 60;
            case WAV24:
                return sr * ch * 3 * 60;
            case WAV32:
                return sr * ch * 4 * 60;
            case AMR_NB:
                // 12.2 kbps mono regardless of preset.
                return 12200L * 60 / 8;
            case AMR_WB:
                // 23.85 kbps mono regardless of preset.
                return 23850L * 60 / 8;
            case OPUS: {
                // FormatConverter clamps Opus to [32k, 256k].
                long clamped = Math.max(32000, Math.min(256000,
                        br <= 0 ? 128000 : br));
                return clamped * 60 / 8;
            }
            case FLAC:
                // Android's FLAC encoder takes 16-bit PCM input; typical
                // music compresses to ~55% of that.
                return (long) (sr * ch * 2 * 60 * FLAC_RATIO);
            case M4A:
            case AUTO:
            default: {
                long clamped = Math.max(64000, Math.min(320000, br));
                return clamped * 60 / 8;
            }
        }
    }

    /** Lossless-compression ratio used for the FLAC estimate. */
    private static final double FLAC_RATIO = 0.55d;

    /** True when the size estimate is content-dependent rather than fixed-rate. */
    public boolean sizeIsApproximate() {
        return this == FLAC || this == AUTO;
    }

    /**
     * Short human label for the format picker ("~1.9 MB/min", "17 MB/min").
     * Prefixed with {@code ~} when the rate is content-dependent so variable
     * formats never look like a promise.
     */
    public String sizePerMinuteLabel(RecordPreset preset) {
        long bpm = bytesPerMinute(preset);
        double mb = bpm / (1024.0 * 1024.0);
        String prefix = sizeIsApproximate() ? "~" : "";
        if (mb >= 9.95) {
            return String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "%s%.0f MB/min",
                    prefix, mb);
        }
        return String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "%s%.1f MB/min",
                prefix, mb);
    }
}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FILE: app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/RecordPreset.java
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
package com.example.hello;

import android.content.Context;
import android.content.SharedPreferences;
import android.media.MediaRecorder;

/**
 * The three recording presets. Each one is a distinct capture geometry —
 * mono vs stereo, processed mic vs unprocessed — so none overlaps another.
 * Containers live in {@link SaveFormat}: "Raw Studio" as a preset was just
 * Music-plus-WAV, and "Voice vs Standard" was one mono capture at two
 * bitrates, so both collapsed away. Everything is locked to 48&nbsp;kHz so
 * AudioFlinger never has to resample, and Music uses the UNPROCESSED source
 * to bypass AGC ducking and effects.
 */
public enum RecordPreset {
    MEMO("memo", R.string.preset_memo, R.string.preset_memo_sub,
            "MEMO 96k", 1, 96000, MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC),
    PODCAST("podcast", R.string.preset_podcast, R.string.preset_podcast_sub,
            "POD 256k", 2, 256000, MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC),
    MUSIC("music", R.string.preset_music, R.string.preset_music_sub,
            "MUS 320k", 2, 320000, MediaRecorder.AudioSource.UNPROCESSED, true);

    public final String id;
    public final int titleRes;
    public final int subRes;
    /** Short badge text, e.g. "MUS 320k". */
    public final String shortLabel;
    /** 1 = mono, 2 = stereo (before any mono fallback). */
    public final int channels;
    /** AAC bitrate for the save conversion. */
    public final int aacBitrate;
    public final int audioSource;
    /**
     * True when the capture should be kept lossless by default. Only the
     * unprocessed stereo master qualifies: AAC is transparent for speech but
     * discards real detail in a music take, so AUTO saves Music as 32-bit
     * float WAV (WAV32) rather than squeezing it through a lossy codec.
     */
    public final boolean autoSavesLossless;

    RecordPreset(String id, int titleRes, int subRes, String shortLabel,
                 int channels, int aacBitrate, int audioSource) {
        this(id, titleRes, subRes, shortLabel, channels, aacBitrate,
                audioSource, false);
    }

    RecordPreset(String id, int titleRes, int subRes, String shortLabel,
                 int channels, int aacBitrate, int audioSource,
                 boolean autoSavesLossless) {
        this.id = id;
        this.titleRes = titleRes;
        this.subRes = subRes;
        this.shortLabel = shortLabel;
        this.channels = channels;
        this.aacBitrate = aacBitrate;
        this.audioSource = audioSource;
        this.autoSavesLossless = autoSavesLossless;
    }

    public boolean wantsStereo() {
        return channels == 2;
    }

    public boolean wantsUnprocessed() {
        return audioSource == MediaRecorder.AudioSource.UNPROCESSED;
    }

    public static RecordPreset of(String id) {
        if (id != null) {
            for (RecordPreset p : values()) {
                if (p.id.equals(id)) return p;
            }
            // Retired presets map to their closest surviving capture.
            if ("voice".equals(id) || "standard".equals(id)) return MEMO;
            if ("raw".equals(id)) return MUSIC;
        }
        return MEMO;
    }

    public static RecordPreset[] all() {
        return values();
    }

    private static final String PREFS = "takeone";
    private static final String KEY = "rec_preset";

    public static RecordPreset load(Context ctx) {
        try {
            SharedPreferences p = ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE);
            return of(p.getString(KEY, MEMO.id));
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return MEMO;
        }
    }

    public void save(Context ctx) {
        try {
            ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                    .edit().putString(KEY, id).apply();
        } catch (Exception ignored) {}
    }
}

    &lt;string name=&quot;fmt_wav16_sub&quot;&gt;16-bit PCM • 48 kHz&lt;/string&gt;
