    @Test
    public void pauseResumeKeepsStreamAdoptable() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx, "Streaming Pause", 2);
        File adopted = null;
        try {
            engine.beginStreaming(ctx, RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A);
            assertNotNull(engine.streaming());
            engine.startCapture(ctx,
                    android.media.MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC);
            Thread.sleep(1500);
            engine.pauseCapture();
            // Encoder idles while paused; resume must continue the same
            // stream with contiguous timestamps.
            Thread.sleep(800);
            engine.resumeCapture(ctx,
                    android.media.MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC);
            Thread.sleep(1500);
            engine.pauseCapture();
            assertTrue("streaming died across pause: "
                    + (engine.streaming() != null
                            ? engine.streaming().failure() : "gone"),
                    engine.streaming() != null
                            && engine.streaming().healthy());
            ConversionJobs.SaveResult r = ConversionJobs.dispatchSave(ctx,
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, null);
            assertTrue("paused/resumed stream was not adopted", r.adopted);
            adopted = r.file;
            FormatConverter.validateFinal(adopted, SaveFormat.M4A);
            // ~3s of audio across the pause gap (gap itself not recorded).
            assertTrue("duration=" + r.durationMs,
                    r.durationMs >= 2000 && r.durationMs <= 5000);
        } finally {
            engine.clearSession();
            if (adopted != null && adopted.exists()) {
                // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
                adopted.delete();
            }
            engine.abortAndDelete();
        }
    }
}

    @Test
    public void recordStartsCapture() throws Exception {
        Activity a = openStudio();
        try {
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap));
            long t0 = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
            boolean recording = false;
            while (android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < 4000) {
                if (RecordingEngine.get().state
                        == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING) {
                    recording = true;
                    break;
                }

            }

    }

    @Test
    public void recordStopSaveLandsAdoptedInLibrary() throws Exception {
        Activity a = openStudio();
        UiDevice device = UiDevice.getInstance(
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation());
        try {
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap));
            long t0 = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
            boolean recording = false;
            while (android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < 4000) {
                if (RecordingEngine.get().state
                        == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING) {
                    recording = true;
                    break;
                }
                Thread.sleep(200);
            }
            org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue("no audio input on this device",
                    recording);
            Thread.sleep(2500);
            // Stop -> save dialog -> Save -> adopted save -> library.
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabStopWrap));
            UiObject save = device.findObject(new UiSelector().text("Save"));
            assertTrue("save dialog never appeared", save.waitForExists(5000));
            save.click();
            // Adopted save exits the studio quickly; the library row with
            // our take name must exist.
            boolean landed = false;
            t0 = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
            while (android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < 15000) {
                if (findByText(a.getWindow().getDecorView(), "Flow Take")
                        != null) {
                    landed = true;
                    break;
                }
                Thread.sleep(500);
            }
            assertTrue("saved take never landed in the library", landed);
        } finally {
            try {
                for (Take t : TakesRepository.all()) {
                    if ("Flow Take".equals(t.title)) {
                        TakesRepository.delete(t.id);
                    }
                }
            } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            RecordingEngine.get().abortAndDelete();
        }
    }

    private static View findByText(View v, String needle) {
        if (v instanceof TextView) {
            CharSequence cs = ((TextView) v).getText();
            if (cs != null && needle.equals(cs.toString().trim())) return v;
        }
        if (v instanceof android.view.ViewGroup) {
            android.view.ViewGroup g = (android.view.ViewGroup) v;
            for (int i = 0; i < g.getChildCount(); i++) {
                View hit = findByText(g.getChildAt(i), needle);
                if (hit != null) return hit;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    @Test
    public void backDuringRecordingSwitchesDirectlyToBackground() throws Exception {
        Activity a = openStudio();
        UiDevice device = UiDevice.getInstance(
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation());
        try {
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap));
            long t0 = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
            boolean recording = false;
            while (android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < 4000) {
                if (RecordingEngine.get().state
                        == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING) {
                    recording = true;
                    break;
                }
                Thread.sleep(200);
            }
            org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue("no audio input on this device",
                    recording);
            // Back arrow switches to background recording in Library with no modal.
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.backBtn));
            Thread.sleep(1000);
            assertTrue(RecordingEngine.get().state
                    == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING);
            assertNotNull(findByText(a.getWindow().getDecorView(),
                    "Library"));
            // Reopen and discard to leave no trace.
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap));
            Thread.sleep(1000);
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabStopWrap));
            UiObject discard = device.findObject(
                    new UiSelector().text("Discard"));
            assertTrue("no discard option", discard.waitForExists(5000));
            discard.click();
            Thread.sleep(1500);
            assertTrue(!RecordingEngine.get().hasSession());
        } finally {
            RecordingEngine.get().abortAndDelete();
        }
    }

    @Test
    public void audioFocusLossPausesAndNeverResumes() throws Exception {
        // A phone call manifests to the app as audio-focus loss; the
        // contract is pause now, never resume on your own.
        Activity a = openStudio();
        try {
            uiTap(a, a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap));
            long t0 = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
            boolean recording = false;
            while (android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < 4000) {
                if (RecordingEngine.get().state
                        == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING) {
                    recording = true;
                    break;
                }
                Thread.sleep(200);
            }
            org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue("no audio input on this device",
                    recording);
            // Outlive the focus-loss grace window after capture start.
            Thread.sleep(1500);
            android.media.AudioManager am =
                    (android.media.AudioManager) a.getSystemService(
                            android.content.Context.AUDIO_SERVICE);
            android.media.AudioManager.OnAudioFocusChangeListener probe =
                    focus -> { };
            int res = am.requestAudioFocus(probe,
                    android.media.AudioManager.STREAM_MUSIC,
                    android.media.AudioManager.AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN);
            assertEquals(android.media.AudioManager.AUDIOFOCUS_REQUEST_GRANTED,
                    res);
            try {
                long t1 = android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
                boolean paused = false;
                while (android.os.SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t1 < 5000) {
                    if (RecordingEngine.get().state
                            == RecordingEngine.State.PAUSED) {
                        paused = true;
                        break;
                    }
                    Thread.sleep(200);
                }
                assertTrue("focus loss did not pause capture", paused);
                // Hand focus back: the app must NOT resume by itself.
                am.abandonAudioFocus(probe);
                Thread.sleep(2500);
                assertTrue("capture auto-resumed after focus returned",
                        RecordingEngine.get().state
                                == RecordingEngine.State.PAUSED);
            } finally {
                am.abandonAudioFocus(probe);
            }
        } finally {
            RecordingEngine.get().abortAndDelete();
        }
    }
}

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/SyntheticVoiceCaptureTest.java
=================================================================================
package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Rule;
import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.nio.ByteOrder;

/**
 * Proves the emulator's virtual microphone is actually engaged: records a few
 * seconds while the host plays generated speech into the mic, then asserts
 * the captured float WAV contains real signal (not silence/zeros) and that
 * the engine's live level meter responds.
 *
 * <p>Run {@code adb emu avd rewindaudio} just before this class so the
 * file-backed mic starts at the beginning of the speech sample.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class SyntheticVoiceCaptureTest {

    @Rule
    public androidx.test.rule.GrantPermissionRule mic =
            androidx.test.rule.GrantPermissionRule.grant(
                    android.Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO);

    /**
     * True when the device offers a usable capture input.
     *
     * <p>This test needs a real audio source behind the mic: the emulator's
     * virtual mic, fed by the host. On a runner with no audio backend the HAL
     * rejects the input format outright ("getInputBufferSize:
     * INVALID_ARGUMENTS"), and there is nothing to assert about the app in
     * that case.
     */
    private boolean captureInputAvailable(Context ctx) {
        android.media.AudioManager am =
                (android.media.AudioManager) ctx.getSystemService(
                        Context.AUDIO_SERVICE);
        if (am == null) return false;
        android.media.AudioDeviceInfo[] ins =
                am.getDevices(android.media.AudioManager.GET_DEVICES_INPUTS);
        if (ins == null || ins.length == 0) return false;
        // Opening a record is not proof of a source: on a host with no audio
        // backend the HAL hands back an initialised record that never
        // produces a sample. Read briefly and require real energy.
        android.media.AudioRecord rec = null;
        try {
            int min = android.media.AudioRecord.getMinBufferSize(48000,
                    android.media.AudioFormat.CHANNEL_IN_MONO,
                    android.media.AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_FLOAT);
            if (min <= 0) min = 8192;
            rec = new android.media.AudioRecord(
                    android.media.MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC, 48000,
                    android.media.AudioFormat.CHANNEL_IN_MONO,
                    android.media.AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_FLOAT,
                    min * 2);
            if (rec.getState() != android.media.AudioRecord.STATE_INITIALIZED) {
                return false;
            }
            rec.startRecording();
            if (rec.getRecordingState()
                    != android.media.AudioRecord.RECORDSTATE_RECORDING) {
                return false;
            }
            float peak = 0f;
            byte[] buf = new byte[4096];
            long until = System.currentTimeMillis() + 1200;
            while (System.currentTimeMillis() < until && peak < 0.001f) {
                int n = rec.read(buf, 0, buf.length);
                if (n <= 0) continue;
                ByteBuffer bb = ByteBuffer.wrap(buf, 0, n)
                        .order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
                while (bb.remaining() >= 4) {
                    float v = Math.abs(bb.getFloat());
                    if (v > peak) peak = v;
                }
            }
            return peak > 0.001f;
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            return false;
        } finally {
            if (rec != null) {
                try {
                    rec.stop();
                } catch (Throwable ignored) {}
                try {
                    rec.release();
                } catch (Throwable ignored) {}
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    public void virtualMicCapturesGeneratedSpeech() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue("no usable capture input on this device",
                captureInputAvailable(ctx));
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx, "Synthetic Voice", 2);
        try {
            engine.startCapture(ctx,
                    android.media.MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC);
            assertTrue("capture did not start",
                    engine.state == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING);

            // Let ~2.5s of the generated speech stream in.
            Thread.sleep(2500);

            float level = engine.level;
            assertTrue("live meter never moved; mic is silent (level="
                    + level + ")", level > 0.001f);

            File raw = engine.finalizeRaw();
            assertTrue("no raw file", raw != null && raw.exists());

            float peak = 0f;
            double sum = 0d;
            long n = 0;
            RandomAccessFile r = new RandomAccessFile(raw, "r");
            try {
                r.seek(44);
                byte[] buf = new byte[65536];
                ByteBuffer bb = ByteBuffer.wrap(buf)
                        .order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
                int read;
                while ((read = r.read(buf)) > 0) {
                    bb.clear();
                    bb.limit(read);
                    while (bb.remaining() >= 4) {
                        float s = Math.abs(bb.getFloat());
                        if (s > peak) peak = s;
                        sum += s;
                        n++;
                    }
                }
            } finally {
                r.close();
            }
            double mean = n == 0 ? 0 : sum / n;
            assertTrue("captured only " + n + " samples", n > 48000);
            assertTrue("captured silence (peak=" + peak + ", mean=" + mean
                    + "); the virtual mic is not engaged",
                    peak > 0.02f && mean > 0.0005);

            // And the synthetic take must survive the real save pipeline.
            TakeSaver.Result result = TakeSaver.finalizeAndConvert(ctx,
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, null);
            assertTrue("no saved file",
                    result != null && result.file.exists()
                            && result.file.length() > 512);
            // noinspection ResultOfMethodCallIgnored
            result.file.delete();
        } finally {
            engine.abortAndDelete();
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;

/**
 * NEW-03 on device: conversions encode into {@code .part} first and only a
 * validated container is renamed to its final name — a kill mid-conversion
 * can never leave a corrupt final file, and no stray part survives success.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class TakeSaverPartTest {

    private File makeRaw(Context ctx, String name) throws Exception {
        File takes = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx);
        File f = new File(takes, name + "_" + System.nanoTime() + ".wav");
        int frames = 48000 * 2;
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, (long) frames * 2 * 4));
            float[] buf = new float[frames * 2];
            for (int i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
                buf[i] = (float) Math.sin(i * 0.05) * 0.4f;
            }
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(w, buf, 0, buf.length);
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    @Test
    public void convertRawAdoptsValidatedPartOnly() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        File raw = makeRaw(ctx, "PartLife");
        File fin = null;
        try {
            TakeSaver.Result r = TakeSaver.convertRaw(ctx, raw, "Part Life",
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.WAV16, null);
            fin = r.file;
            assertNotNull("no result file", fin);
            assertTrue("final file missing", fin.exists());
            assertTrue("final file too small", fin.length() > 1024);
            assertTrue("stray part survived success",
                    !ConversionJob.partFor(raw).exists());
            // Nothing half-written under a final-looking name either.
            FormatConverter.validateFinal(fin, SaveFormat.WAV16);
        } finally {
            if (fin != null && fin.exists()) fin.delete();
            File part = ConversionJob.partFor(raw);
            if (part.exists()) part.delete();
            if (raw.exists()) raw.delete();
        }
    }

    @Test
    public void convertRawFailureLeavesNoStrays() throws Exception {
        Context ctx = InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation()
                .getTargetContext();
        File raw = new File(RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx),
                "PartFail_" + System.nanoTime() + ".wav");
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(raw, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(new byte[100]); // not a WAV at all
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        boolean threw = false;
        try {
            TakeSaver.convertRaw(ctx, raw, "Part Fail",
                    RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, null);
        } catch (Exception expected) {
            threw = true;
        }
        try {
            assertTrue("garbage raw must fail conversion", threw);
            assertTrue("stray part survived failure",
                    !ConversionJob.partFor(raw).exists());
        } finally {
            if (raw.exists()) raw.delete();
            File part = ConversionJob.partFor(raw);
            if (part.exists()) part.delete();
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Opens the teleprompter dialogs against a real Activity on a real Android
 * image.

 * reproduces with a genuine window — Robolectric covers the ordering, this
 * covers the real thing.

@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class TeleDialogsDeviceTest {

    private Activity launch() {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        Intent i = new Intent(instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        return instr.startActivitySync(i);
    }

    @Test
    public void editorOpensOnRealDevice() {
        final Activity a = launch();
        a.runOnUiThread(() -> {
            TeleDialogs.showEditor(a, "line one\nline two", 120,
                    text -> { }, null);
        });
        InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
        // Reaching here without an exception is the assertion: the old code
        // threw requestFeature() must be called before adding content.
    }

    public void appSurvivesOpeningEditorTwice() {
        Activity a = launch();
        a.runOnUiThread(() -> {
            TeleDialogs.showEditor(a, "script", 120, text -> { }, null);
        });
        InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
        a.runOnUiThread(() -> {
            TeleDialogs.showEditor(a, "script two", 120, text -> { }, null);
        });
        InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
        assertTrue("activity died while dialogs were open",
                !a.isFinishing() && !a.isDestroyed());
    }

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.ViewGroup;
import android.widget.TextView;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * On-device checks for the prompter rework: centring, stable wrapping, the
 * windowed render, and the inline four-way controls.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class TeleprompterDisplayTest {

    private Activity launch() {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        return instr.startActivitySync(i);
    }

    private static String manyWords(int n) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (i > 0) sb.append(' ');
            sb.append("word").append(i);
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    @Test
    public void splitsScriptIntoSegmentsThatCoverEveryWord() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);

        int total = 400;
        v.setScript(manyWords(total));
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);

        assertTrue("no segments produced", v.segmentCount() > 0);
        // Every word must survive the split, in order.
        StringBuilder joined = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < v.segmentCount(); i++) {
            String s = v.segmentAt(i);
            if (s == null || s.isEmpty()) continue;
            if (joined.length() > 0) joined.append(' ');
            joined.append(s);
        }
        String[] got = joined.toString().split("\\s+");
        assertEquals("segment split lost or reordered words", total, got.length);
        for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) {
            assertEquals("word " + i + " changed", "word" + i, got[i]);
        }
    }

    @Test
    public void segmentsOutOfRangeAreEmptyNotCrashing() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        v.setScript(manyWords(60));

        // Before the start and past the end must both return "".
        assertEquals("", v.segmentAt(-1));
        assertEquals("", v.segmentAt(v.segmentCount()));
        assertEquals("", v.segmentAt(v.segmentCount() + 500));
    }

    @Test
    public void wrappingIsStableAcrossRedraws() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        v.setScript(manyWords(300));

        List<String> first = snapshot(v);
        // Scroll, force redraws, and confirm the split did not shift. A
        // character-count estimate re-wrapped between passes, which is what
        // made the words appear to flicker.
        for (int i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
            v.scrollBy(17f);
            v.measure(
                    View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                    View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
            v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        }
        assertEquals("segments changed while scrolling", first, snapshot(v));
    }

    private static List<String> snapshot(TeleprompterView v) {
        List<String> out = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < v.segmentCount(); i++) out.add(v.segmentAt(i));
        return out;
    }

    @Test
    public void lastLineCanReachTheCentreLine() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        v.setScript(manyWords(500));

        v.setScrollOffset(Float.MAX_VALUE);
        assertTrue("nothing scrollable", v.maxScroll() > 0f);
        float lh = v.lineHeight();
        // At full scroll the last segment must land on the centre line.
        float centreLine = h / 2f + lh * 0.36f;
        float lastBaseline = h / 2f - v.maxScroll()
                + (v.segmentCount() - 1) * lh;
        assertEquals("last line did not reach the centre line",
                centreLine, lastBaseline, 2f);
        // And it must be comfortably inside the viewport, not clipped.
        assertTrue("last line is below the viewport", lastBaseline < h);
        assertTrue("last line is above the viewport", lastBaseline > 0f);
    }

    @Test
    public void textIsHorizontallyCentred() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        v.setScript(manyWords(50));

        android.graphics.Bitmap bmp = android.graphics.Bitmap
                .createBitmap(w, h, android.graphics.Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888);
        android.graphics.Canvas c = new android.graphics.Canvas(bmp);
        v.draw(c);

        // Ink in the first 40px would mean the text hugs the left padding.
        int farLeft = inked(bmp, 0, 40);
        assertEquals("text is flush to the left edge", 0, farLeft);
        int farRight = inked(bmp, w - 40, w);
        assertEquals("text is flush to the right edge", 0, farRight);
        // And there should be ink somewhere in the middle band.
        assertTrue("nothing rendered", inked(bmp, w / 4, w - w / 4) > 0);

        // Symmetry: ink left of centre should roughly mirror ink right of it.
        // A left-aligned prompter shows a large, stable imbalance.
        int left = inked(bmp, 0, w / 2);
        int right = inked(bmp, w / 2, w);
        float skew = Math.abs(left - right) / (float) Math.max(1, left + right);
        assertTrue("ink is not balanced about the centre (skew=" + skew
                + ", left=" + left + ", right=" + right + ")", skew < 0.18f);
    }

    private static int inked(android.graphics.Bitmap b, int x0, int x1) {
        int n = 0;
        for (int x = Math.max(0, x0); x < Math.min(b.getWidth(), x1); x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < b.getHeight(); y += 2) {
                if ((b.getPixel(x, y) & 0xFF000000) != 0) n++;
            }
        }
        return n;
    }

    @Test
    public void studioShowsInlineControlsInsteadOfTuneMenu() {
        Activity a = launch();
        // Inflate the studio layout directly: this asserts the screen's
        // contract without depending on which fragment happens to be
        // on-screen after launch (a name modal or library can be showing).
        View root = android.view.LayoutInflater.from(a)
                .inflate(R.layout.fragment_studio, null, false);
        assertNotNullId(root, R.id.teleSizeValue);
        assertNotNullId(root, R.id.teleSpeedValue);
        assertNotNullId(root, R.id.teleWplValue);
        assertNotNullId(root, R.id.telePauseBtn);
        assertNotNullId(root, R.id.zoomValue);
        // The separate tuning entry point is gone from the studio screen.
        assertTrue("Tune button still present",
                findByText(root, "Tune") == null);
    }

    /** Depth-first search for a visible TextView with the given label. */
    private static View findByText(View v, String needle) {
        if (v instanceof TextView) {
            CharSequence cs = ((TextView) v).getText();
            if (cs != null
                    && needle.equals(cs.toString().trim())) {
                return v;
            }
        }
        if (v instanceof ViewGroup) {
            ViewGroup g = (ViewGroup) v;
            for (int i = 0; i < g.getChildCount(); i++) {
                View hit = findByText(g.getChildAt(i), needle);
                if (hit != null) return hit;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static void assertNotNullId(View root, int id) {
        if (root.findViewById(id) == null) {
            throw new AssertionError("missing view id " + id);
        }
    }

    @Test
    public void teleValueStepsAndReports() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleValue tv = new TeleValue(a);
        tv.configure(10, 20, 1, 15, "");
        final int[] seen = {-1};
        tv.setOnValueChanged(v -> seen[0] = v);
        assertEquals(15, tv.getValue());
        tv.setValue(16, true);
        assertEquals(16, tv.getValue());
        assertEquals(16, seen[0]);
        // Clamped to the configured range.
        tv.setValue(999, true);
        assertEquals(20, tv.getValue());
        tv.setValue(-999, true);
        assertEquals(10, tv.getValue());
    }

    @Test
    public void zoomMinimumFollowsTimelineLength() {
        Activity a = launch();
        WaveformView wv = new WaveformView(a);
        int minShort = Math.round(wv.minimumZoom() * 100f);
        for (int i = 0; i < 4000; i++) wv.push(0.5f);
        int minLong = Math.round(wv.minimumZoom() * 100f);
        assertEquals("history did not grow", 4000, wv.historyCount());
        assertTrue("minimum zoom did not drop for a longer timeline",
                minLong < minShort);
        // And the floor must never be above the old fixed 0.5.
        assertTrue("minimum zoom exceeds the old cap",
                wv.minimumZoom() <= 0.5f);
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.view.MotionEvent;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.ViewConfiguration;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

/**
 * Regression cover for the prompter appearing "dead": no scrolling, and the
 * script stopping after the first screenful.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class TeleprompterScrollBoundsTest {

    private Activity launch() {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        return instr.startActivitySync(i);
    }

    private static String manyWords(int n) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (i > 0) sb.append(' ');
            sb.append("word").append(i);
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    /**
     * The exact ordering the real screen uses: script is assigned before the
     * view has a size. The scroll bounds were computed at height 0 and then
     * never recomputed, leaving maxScroll at 0.
     */
    @Test
    public void scriptSetBeforeLayoutStillGetsScrollBounds() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);

        // No measure/layout yet: width and height are both 0.
        v.setScript(manyWords(400));
        assertEquals("precondition: unlaid view has no bounds",
                0f, v.maxScroll(), 0.01f);

        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);

        assertTrue("maxScroll stayed 0 after layout, so the script cannot "
                + "be scrolled past the first screenful", v.maxScroll() > 0f);

        // And it must actually be able to reach the end.
        v.setScrollOffset(Float.MAX_VALUE);
        assertEquals("did not reach the end", v.maxScroll(),
                v.scrollOffset(), 0.01f);
        assertTrue("end of script is at the top of the view",
                v.scrollOffset() > 0f);
    }

    @Test
    public void resizingKeepsScrollBoundsValid() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(900, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(600, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, 900, 600);
        v.setScript(manyWords(400));
        float before = v.maxScroll();
        assertTrue("no scroll range when laid out", before > 0f);

        // Panel height does not change where the tail has to stop, so the
        // range is stable; what matters is that it stays reachable and that a
        // position from the old height is re-clamped into the new bounds.
        v.scrollBy(100000f);
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(900, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(300, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, 900, 300);
        assertTrue("scroll range vanished after resize", v.maxScroll() > 0f);
        v.scrollBy(100000f);
        assertTrue("offset exceeded bounds after resize",
                v.scrollOffset() <= v.maxScroll() + 0.5f);
        assertTrue("offset left the script", v.scrollOffset() > 0f);
    }

    @Test
    public void draggingTheScriptScrollsIt() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        v.setScript(manyWords(400));

        final float before = v.scrollOffset();
        // Drag upward: the text follows the finger, revealing later lines.
        v.onTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 300f, 300f));
        for (float y = 290f; y >= 110f; y -= 20f) {
            v.onTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, 450f, y));
        }
        v.onTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, 450f, 110f));
        assertTrue("a drag did not scroll the script (" + before + " -> "
                + v.scrollOffset() + ")", v.scrollOffset() > before + 1f);
    }

    @Test
    public void draggingBackReturnsToTheTop() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleprompterView v = new TeleprompterView(a);
        int w = 900, h = 600;
        v.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        v.layout(0, 0, w, h);
        v.setScript(manyWords(400));

        v.scrollBy(150f);
        assertTrue("could not scroll down before dragging back",
                v.scrollOffset() > 100f);
        v.onTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 450f, 150f));
        for (float y = 450f; y <= 550f; y += 20f) {
            v.onTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, 450f, y));
        }
        v.onTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, 450f, 550f));
        assertEquals("dragging back did not return to the top",
                0f, v.scrollOffset(), 0.5f);
    }

    /**
     * The prompter must have real height on the actual studio screen. It once
     * collapsed to 0px because the fixed content below overran the layout, so
     * nothing was drawn and nothing could scroll.
     */
    @Test
    public void prompterHasUsableHeightOnTheRealScreen() throws Exception {
        // Pre-seed a session so the studio opens directly: the name dialog
        // otherwise stays up and the activity behind it never lays out fully.
        // Also seed a long script so there is somewhere to scroll to.
        android.content.Context ctx =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext();
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx, "Instrumentation", 2);
        ctx.getSharedPreferences("takeone", android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                .edit().putString("tele_script", manyWords(400)).apply();
        TeleSettings.invalidateCache();
        try {
            Activity a = launch();
            View fab = a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap);
            if (fab != null) {
                a.runOnUiThread(fab::performClick);
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
            }
            final TeleprompterView tele =
                    (TeleprompterView) a.findViewById(R.id.teleView);
            assertTrue("prompter not found", tele != null);
            InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
            android.os.SystemClock.sleep(300);

            // The regression was a prompter with no height at all: nothing
            // drawn, and maxScroll stuck at 0 so it could never scroll.
            assertTrue("prompter collapsed to " + tele.getHeight() + "px; "
                            + describe(tele), tele.getHeight() > 0);
        assertTrue("prompter cannot scroll (max=" + tele.maxScroll() + ")",
                tele.maxScroll() > 0f);
        // It must actually show lines, not a single sliver.
        int lines = tele.visibleLineCount();
        assertTrue("only " + lines + " line(s) fit at "
                + tele.getHeight() + "px", lines >= 3);
        // And it must win a real share of its panel, rather than being left
        // with only what the header and controls did not need.
        android.view.View panel = (android.view.View) tele.getParent();
        assertTrue("prompter is " + tele.getHeight() + "px of a "
                + panel.getHeight() + "px panel",
                tele.getHeight() * 3 >= panel.getHeight());
        } finally {
            engine.abortAndDelete();
            ctx.getSharedPreferences("takeone",
                    android.content.Context.MODE_PRIVATE).edit()
                    .remove("tele_script").remove("tele_auto").commit();
            TeleSettings.invalidateCache();
        }
    }

    /**
     * The reading centre must sit in the middle of the *visible* area: the
     * control chrome overlays the top of the panel, so the view shifts its
     * centre down by half the chrome height.
     */
    @Test
    public void readingCentreAccountsForOverlaidChrome() throws Exception {
        android.content.Context ctx =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext();
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        engine.startNewSession(ctx, "Instrumentation", 2);
        try {
            Activity a = launch();
            View fab = a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap);
            if (fab != null) {
                a.runOnUiThread(fab::performClick);
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();

            final TeleprompterView tele =
                    (TeleprompterView) a.findViewById(R.id.teleView);

            final View chrome = a.findViewById(R.id.teleChrome);
            assertTrue("chrome overlay missing", chrome != null);

            android.os.SystemClock.sleep(300);

            java.lang.reflect.Field f = TeleprompterView.class
                    .getDeclaredField("centerShiftPx");
            f.setAccessible(true);
            float shift = (Float) f.get(tele);
            float expect = chrome.getHeight() / 2f;
            assertEquals("reading centre does not account for the chrome",

        } finally {

        }
    }

    /** Walks up the tree so a collapsed ancestor is obvious. */
    static String describe(android.view.View v0) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("chain: ");
        android.view.View cur = v0;
        int guard = 0;
        while (cur != null && guard++ < 7) {
            sb.append(cur.getClass().getSimpleName()).append("[")
              .append(cur.getWidth()).append("x").append(cur.getHeight())
              .append("] < ");
            if (cur.getParent() instanceof android.view.View) {
                cur = (android.view.View) cur.getParent();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private MotionEvent motion(int action, float x, float y) {
        long t = android.os.SystemClock.uptimeMillis();
        return MotionEvent.obtain(t, t, action, x, y, 0);
    }

    /**
     * The inline stepper must respond to a horizontal drag even though its
     * children are clickable and consume the initial touch.
     */
    @Test
    public void inlineStepperScrubsOnHorizontalDrag() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleValue tv = new TeleValue(a);
        tv.configure(10, 100, 1, 50, "");
        final int[] live = {-1};
        final int[] finished = {-1};
        final int[] discrete = {-1};
        tv.setOnScrubListener(new TeleValue.OnScrubListener() {
            @Override public void onScrubValueChanged(int v) {
                live[0] = v;
            }

            @Override public void onScrubFinished(int v) {
                finished[0] = v;
            }
        });
        tv.setOnValueChanged(v -> discrete[0] = v);

        int w = 200, h = 40;
        tv.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(w, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(h, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        tv.layout(0, 0, w, h);

        long t = android.os.SystemClock.uptimeMillis();
        tv.dispatchTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 100f, 20f));
        for (float x = 104f; x <= 160f; x += 6f) {
            tv.dispatchTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, x, 21f));
        }
        assertTrue("horizontal drag did not change the value live (still "
                + tv.getValue() + ")", live[0] > 50);
        tv.dispatchTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, 160f, 21f));

        assertEquals("scrub did not report its final value",
                tv.getValue(), finished[0]);
        assertEquals("a scrub must not also fire the discrete tap listener",
                -1, discrete[0]);
    }

    @Test
    public void inlineStepperIgnoresVerticalDrag() {
        Activity a = launch();
        TeleValue tv = new TeleValue(a);
        tv.configure(10, 100, 1, 50, "");
        tv.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(200, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(40, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        tv.layout(0, 0, 200, 40);

        tv.dispatchTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 100f, 10f));
        for (float y = 12f; y <= 38f; y += 6f) {
            tv.dispatchTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, 101f, y));
        }
        tv.dispatchTouchEvent(motion(MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL, 101f, 38f));
        assertEquals("a vertical drag must not change the value",
                50, tv.getValue());
    }

FILE: app/src/androidTest/java/com/example/hello/TeleprompterScrollStartTest.java

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertNotNull;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.content.Context;
import android.os.SystemClock;
import android.view.View;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Rule;
import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import androidx.test.rule.GrantPermissionRule;

/**
 * Proves the prompter starts moving with the recording.
 *
 * <p>The complaint was that the script sat still for several seconds after
 * hitting record — the countdown was gating the scroll, so the take began
 * before the text did.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
public class TeleprompterScrollStartTest {

    @Rule
    public GrantPermissionRule mic = GrantPermissionRule.grant(
            android.Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO);

    /**
     * The studio capture path also gates on POST_NOTIFICATIONS (SDK 33+):
     * without it the fab opens a rationale instead of recording. Grant it
     * once per class so these tests verify recording instead of skipping.
     */
    @org.junit.BeforeClass
    public static void grantNotifForUiRecording() {
        if (android.os.Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33) {
            try {
                androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry
                        .getInstrumentation().getUiAutomation()
                        .executeShellCommand("pm grant "
                                + androidx.test.platform.app
                                        .InstrumentationRegistry
                                        .getInstrumentation()
                                        .getTargetContext().getPackageName()
                                + " android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS");
            } catch (Exception ignored) {}
        }
    }

    /** True if the prompter scrolled at all within the window. */
    private boolean scrollMovedBy(TeleprompterView tele, Activity a, long ms) {
        float f = tele.scrollOffset();
        long t0 = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
        while (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < ms) {
            SystemClock.sleep(150);
            InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
            if (tele.scrollOffset() > f + 1f) return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    /** Walks up the tree so a collapsed ancestor is obvious. */
    private static String describe(TeleprompterView v) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        sb.append("script=").append(v.getScript() == null
                ? -1 : v.getScript().length())
          .append(" segments=").append(v.segmentCount())
          .append(" max=").append(v.maxScroll()).append(" | chain: ");
        android.view.View cur = v;
        int guard = 0;
        while (cur != null && guard++ < 6) {
            sb.append(cur.getClass().getSimpleName())
              .append("[vis=").append(cur.getVisibility())
              .append(" ").append(cur.getWidth()).append("x")
              .append(cur.getHeight())
              .append(android.view.View.VISIBLE == cur.getVisibility()
                      ? "" : " HIDDEN")
              .append("] < ");
            if (cur.getParent() instanceof android.view.View) {
                cur = (android.view.View) cur.getParent();
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private static String manyWords(int n) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (i > 0) sb.append(' ');
            sb.append("line").append(i).append(" of the script text");
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private Activity launch() {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        return instr.startActivitySync(i);
    }

    /** Clicks into the studio, clearing the "name this take" prompt if shown. */
    private TeleprompterView gotoStudio(Activity a) throws Exception {
        // Pre-seed a session so the studio opens directly without the name
        // dialog (which otherwise keeps the activity from laying out fully).
        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        engine.startNewSession(
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().getTargetContext(),
                "Instrumentation", 2);
        View fab = a.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap);
        if (fab != null) {
            a.runOnUiThread(fab::performClick);
            InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
        }
        return (TeleprompterView) a.findViewById(R.id.teleView);
    }

    /**
     * The regression itself: arming the prompter for a take must not push the
     * countdown into the future, because that is what held the script still
     * after the user pressed record.
     */
    @Test
    public void armingForATakeDoesNotArmACountdown() throws Exception {
        Activity a = launch();
        try {
        TeleprompterView tele = gotoStudio(a);
        assertNotNull("teleprompter not on screen", tele);

        java.lang.reflect.Field f = StudioFragment.class
                .getDeclaredField("teleCountdownUntil");
        f.setAccessible(true);
        StudioFragment frag = studioFragment(a);
        assertNotNull("studio fragment not found", frag);

        java.lang.reflect.Method arm = StudioFragment.class
                .getDeclaredMethod("teleprompterArmForTake");
        arm.setAccessible(true);
        java.lang.reflect.Method park = StudioFragment.class
                .getDeclaredMethod("setTelePaused", boolean.class);
        park.setAccessible(true);
        a.runOnUiThread(() -> {
            try {
                tele.scrollBy(10000f);
                arm.invoke(frag);
                // Arming unpauses so the take scrolls; the live tick would
                // advance the script before the assertion below reads it, so
                // freeze atomically on the same UI-thread pass.
                park.invoke(frag, true);
            } catch (Exception ignored) {
            }
        });
        InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();

        long until = (Long) f.get(frag);
        assertTrue("countdown still blocks the prompter for " + until
                + "ms after record", until <= SystemClock.elapsedRealtime());
        assertTrue("teleprompter should be rewound to the top",
                tele.scrollOffset() == 0f);
        } finally {
            RecordingEngine.get().abortAndDelete();
        }
    }

    private static StudioFragment studioFragment(Activity a) {
        androidx.fragment.app.FragmentManager fm =
                ((androidx.fragment.app.FragmentActivity) a)
                        .getSupportFragmentManager();
        androidx.fragment.app.Fragment frag =
                fm.findFragmentById(R.id.container);
        if (frag == null) {
            for (androidx.fragment.app.Fragment f : fm.getFragments()) {
                if (f instanceof StudioFragment) return (StudioFragment) f;
            }
        }
        return frag instanceof StudioFragment ? (StudioFragment) frag : null;
    }

    @Test
    public void prompterBeginsScrollingWithRecordingNotAfterACountdown() throws Exception {
        Activity a = launch();
        // Seed a script long enough that there is somewhere to scroll to.
        a.getSharedPreferences("takeone", Context.MODE_PRIVATE).edit()
                .putString("tele_script", manyWords(400))
                .putBoolean("tele_auto", true)
                .apply();
        TeleSettings.invalidateCache();

        try {
        // Relaunch so the fragment picks the script up.
        Activity b = launch();
        TeleprompterView tele = gotoStudio(b);
        assertNotNull("teleprompter not on screen", tele);
        // Give layout a beat, then confirm there is scrollable content.
        InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
        SystemClock.sleep(400);
        assertTrue("no scrollable script loaded; " + describe(tele),
                tele.maxScroll() > 0f);

        View fab = b.findViewById(R.id.fabWrap);
        assertNotNull("no record button", fab);
        final boolean[] started = {false};
        b.runOnUiThread(() -> {
            fab.performClick();
            started[0] = true;
        });
        InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
        assertTrue("record tap never ran", started[0]);

        // Automated-test emulator images have no audio input, so capture
        // never reaches RECORDING here. Poll first: a -1 sentinel makes a
        // never-moving prompter fail instead of passing vacuously.
        float first = tele.scrollOffset();
        long t0 = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
        long firstMoveAt = -1L;
        float latest = first;
        StringBuilder trace = new StringBuilder();
        while (SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0 < 6000L) {
            SystemClock.sleep(100);
            InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().waitForIdleSync();
            latest = tele.scrollOffset();
            if (latest > first + 2f) {
                firstMoveAt = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - t0;
                break;
            }
            if (trace.length() < 400) {
                trace.append(String.format(" [off=%.1f max=%.1f vis=%s wpm=%d auto=%s]",
                        latest, tele.maxScroll(),
                        tele.getVisibility() == View.VISIBLE,
                        tele.getWordsPerLine(),
                        TeleSettings.load(b).autoScroll));
            }
        }
        org.junit.Assume.assumeTrue("capture never started (no audio input)",
                RecordingEngine.get().state
                        == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING);
        assertTrue("prompter never started scrolling; trace:" + trace,
                firstMoveAt >= 0L);
        assertTrue("prompter waited " + firstMoveAt
                + "ms before moving; it must move with the recording",
                firstMoveAt < 1500L);
        } finally {
            // Stop capture directly so the emulator is not left recording,
            // without going through the save dialog.
            RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
            try {
                engine.pauseCapture();
            } catch (Exception ignored) {
            }
            engine.abortAndDelete();
            a.getSharedPreferences("takeone", Context.MODE_PRIVATE).edit()
                    .remove("tele_script").remove("tele_auto").commit();
            TeleSettings.invalidateCache();
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import android.content.Context;

import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4;
import androidx.test.platform.app.InstrumentationRegistry;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;

import java.io.File;
import java.io.RandomAccessFile;

/**
 * Kill-resume scaffolding: sets up a slow job and holds the process open
 * while the host kills it mid-flight. The real assertions run host-side
 * (logcat/files); the test itself is designed never to finish normally.
 *
 * <p>A4-15: excluded from the suite with {@code @Ignore}. These tests sleep
 * for 90s + 180s and leave 45s/150s raw takes behind, which stalls every
 * instrumentation run and pollutes takes/ for the tests that follow.
 * To use it: drop the @Ignore, run only this class, kill the app from the
 * host mid-flight, then relaunch and check the sidecars.
 */
@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class)
@org.junit.Ignore("Host-driven kill/resume scaffolding; run manually")
public class TempKillTest {

    private File makeLongRaw(Context ctx, String name, int seconds)
            throws Exception {
        File takes = RecordingEngine.takesDir(ctx);
        File f = new File(takes, name + "_" + System.nanoTime() + ".wav");
        int frames = 48000 * seconds;
        RandomAccessFile w = new RandomAccessFile(f, "rw");
        try {
            w.setLength(0);
            w.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, (long) frames * 2 * 4));
            byte[] chunk = new byte[65536];
            java.util.Random rnd = new java.util.Random(7);
            long left = (long) frames * 2 * 4;
            while (left > 0) {
                int n = (int) Math.min(chunk.length, left);
                rnd.nextBytes(chunk);
                w.write(chunk, 0, n);
                left -= n;
            }
        } finally {
            w.close();
        }
        return f;
    }

    @Test
    public void holdQueuedJob() throws Exception {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        instr.startActivitySync(i);
        Context ctx = instr.getTargetContext();
        File raw = makeLongRaw(ctx, "killq", 45);
        ConversionJob job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx, raw, "Kill Queued",
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.M4A, 45000);
        android.util.Log.i("KILLTEST",
                "queued " + job.jobId + " sleeping");
        Thread.sleep(90000);
        android.util.Log.i("KILLTEST", "survived; done="
                + (ConversionJobs.get(job.jobId) == null));
    }

    @Test
    public void holdRunningJob() throws Exception {
        android.app.Instrumentation instr =
                InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation();
        android.content.Intent i = new android.content.Intent(
                instr.getTargetContext(), MainActivity.class);
        i.addFlags(android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
                | android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK);
        instr.startActivitySync(i);
        Context ctx = instr.getTargetContext();
        File raw = makeLongRaw(ctx, "killr", 150);
        ConversionJob job = ConversionJobs.enqueue(ctx, raw, "Kill Running",
                RecordPreset.MEMO, SaveFormat.AMR_NB, 150000);
        ConversionService.startJob(ctx, job.jobId);
        android.util.Log.i("KILLTEST",
                "running " + job.jobId + " sleeping");
        Thread.sleep(180000);
        android.util.Log.i("KILLTEST", "survived");
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import java.io.File;

/**
 * Stage 4 Amplify: two-pass gain processor with automatic peak scanning and
 * non-clipping clamp unless "Allow Clipping" is enabled.
 */
final class AmplifyProcessor extends AudioProcessor {

    private final FxParameter gain = addParameter(FxParameter.dbParam(
            "amp_gain", "Amplification", -50f, 50f, 0f));
    private final FxParameter newPeak = addParameter(FxParameter.dbParam(
            "amp_peak", "New Peak Amplitude", -40f, 0f, 0f));
    private final FxParameter allowClip = addParameter(FxParameter.boolParam(
            "amp_clip", "Allow Clipping", false));

    private float scannedPeak = -1f;

    AmplifyProcessor() {
    }

    @Override
    public String getId() {
        return "amplify";
    }

    @Override
    public String getTitle() {
        return "Amplify";
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return "Two-pass gain with automatic non-clipping peak scan";
    }

    @Override
    public FxCategory getCategory() {
        return FxCategory.DYNAMICS;
    }

    @Override
    public void prepare(int sampleRate, int channels) {
    }

    @Override
    public void reset() {
        scannedPeak = -1f;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean isAudible() {
        return isEnabled() && (Math.abs(gain.getFloat()) > 0.01f
                || Math.abs(newPeak.getFloat()) > 0.01f
                || allowClip.getBoolean());
    }

    @Override
    public void prepareOffline(File raw, long startFrame, long endFrame,
                               int sampleRate, int channels) throws Exception {
        if (raw == null) return;
        float[] slice = EditEngine.readFloatSelection(raw, startFrame, endFrame);
        if (slice == null || slice.length == 0) return;
        float pk = 0f;
        for (float v : slice) {
            float a = Math.abs(v);
            if (a > pk) pk = a;
        }
        scannedPeak = pk;
    }

    /** Effective linear gain for the scanned (or in-block) peak. */
    float computeEffectiveGainDb(float peakDb) {
        float requested = gain.getFloat();
        float ceiling = newPeak.getFloat();
        if (Math.abs(requested) <= 0.01f && Math.abs(ceiling) > 0.01f) {
            requested = (peakDb > -60f) ? (ceiling - peakDb) : ceiling;
        } else if (Math.abs(requested) <= 0.01f && allowClip.getBoolean()) {
            requested = 1.5f;
        }
        if (!allowClip.getBoolean()) {
            float effCeiling = Math.abs(ceiling) > 0.01f ? ceiling : -0.1f;
            float maxAllowed = effCeiling - peakDb;
            if (requested > maxAllowed && requested > 0f) {
                requested = maxAllowed;
            }
        }
        return requested;
    }

    @Override
    public void processInPlace(float[] buf, int frames, int channels) {
        if (!isEnabled() || buf == null || frames <= 0) return;
        int n = Math.min(buf.length, frames * Math.max(1, channels));
        float pk = scannedPeak;
        if (pk < 0f) {
            pk = 0f;
            for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                float a = Math.abs(buf[i]);
                if (a > pk) pk = a;
            }
        }
        float peakDb = pk > 1e-7f ? Dsp.linToDb(pk) : -120f;
        float effDb = computeEffectiveGainDb(peakDb);
        float lin = Dsp.dbToLin(effDb);
        boolean clipAllowed = allowClip.getBoolean();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            float v = buf[i] * lin;
            if (!clipAllowed) {
                if (v > 0.9885f) v = 0.9885f;
                else if (v < -0.9885f) v = -0.9885f;
            }
            buf[i] = v;
        }
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import java.util.Locale;

/**
 * Stage 7 audio diagnostics: measures peak, true peak, RMS, integrated
 * LUFS, dynamic range, DC offset and the foreground/background contrast,
 * and counts clipped samples.
 *
 * <p>All the maths is pure Java so it can be unit tested without a device.
 */
final class AudioDiagnosticsTool {

    private AudioDiagnosticsTool() {}

    /** Result of a diagnostics run over a region. */
    static final class Report {
        float peakDbfs;
        float truePeakDbfs;
        float rmsDbfs;
        float integratedLufs;
        float dynamicRangeLu;
        float dcOffsetPercent;
        float contrastDb;
        boolean wcagPass;
        int clippedRuns;
        int clippedSamples;

        /** One-line summary for the studio dialog. */
        public String summary() {
            return String.format(Locale.US,
                    "Peak %.1f dBFS • True peak %.1f dBFS • RMS %.1f dBFS"
                            + " • %.1f LUFS • DR %.1f LU • DC %.2f%%"
                            + " • Contrast %.1f dB %s • Clipped runs %d",
                    peakDbfs, truePeakDbfs, rmsDbfs, integratedLufs,
                    dynamicRangeLu, dcOffsetPercent, contrastDb,
                    wcagPass ? "(WCAG AAA pass)" : "(WCAG below AAA)",
                    clippedRuns);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Runs the analysis.
     *
     * @param buf            interleaved region samples
     * @param frames         number of frames
     * @param channels       channel count
     * @param sampleRate     sample rate in Hz
     * @param clipThreshold  consecutive-clipped-sample threshold (1..10)
     */
    static Report analyze(float[] buf, int frames, int channels, int sampleRate,
                          int clipThreshold) {
        Report r = new Report();
        if (buf == null || frames <= 0) return r;
        int ch = Math.max(1, Math.min(2, channels));

        float peak = 0f;
        double sumSq = 0;
        double sum = 0;
        int count = 0;
        for (int f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < ch; c++) {
                float v = buf[f * ch + c];
                float a = Math.abs(v);
                if (a > peak) peak = a;
                sumSq += (double) v * v;
                sum += v;
                count++;
            }
        }
        r.peakDbfs = Dsp.linToDb(peak);
        r.rmsDbfs = (float) (10 * Math.log10(Math.max(1e-12, sumSq / count)));
        r.dcOffsetPercent = (float) (100.0 * Math.abs(sum / count));
        r.truePeakDbfs = truePeakDbfs(buf, frames, ch);

        // Integrated loudness via the same K-weighting path as the
        // loudness normalizer.
        r.integratedLufs = integratedLufs(buf, frames, ch, sampleRate);

        // Dynamic range: crest factor between the 95th and 10th percentile
        // of the frame loudness.
        r.dynamicRangeLu = dynamicRangeLu(buf, frames, ch, sampleRate);

        // Foreground / background contrast: the level difference between the
        // loudest 10 % and the quietest 10 % of 100 ms frames.
        float[] frameDb = frameLevels(buf, frames, ch, sampleRate);
        r.contrastDb = contrastDb(frameDb);
        // WCAG 2.0 AAA asks for at least 15 dB of speech contrast.
        r.wcagPass = r.contrastDb >= 15f;

        // Clipping: runs of consecutive samples at or above 0.9999.
        int thr = Math.max(1, clipThreshold);
        int runs = 0;
        int clippedSamples = 0;
        int runLen = 0;
        for (int f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
            boolean clipped = false;
            for (int c = 0; c < ch; c++) {
                if (Math.abs(buf[f * ch + c]) >= 0.9999f) clipped = true;
            }
            if (clipped) {
                runLen++;
                clippedSamples++;
            } else {
                if (runLen >= thr) runs++;
                runLen = 0;
            }
        }
        if (runLen >= thr) runs++;
        r.clippedRuns = runs;
        r.clippedSamples = clippedSamples;
        return r;
    }

    /** 4x oversampled true-peak estimate in dBFS. */
    static float truePeakDbfs(float[] buf, int frames, int ch) {
        float peak = 0f;
        for (int f = 0; f < frames; f++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < ch; c++) {
                float v = buf[f * ch + c];
                float a = Math.abs(v);
                if (a > peak) peak = a;
                // Linear interpolation towards the next sample.
                if (f + 1 < frames) {
                    float n = buf[(f + 1) * ch + c];
                    float inter = Math.abs(v + 0.5f * (n - v));
                    if (inter > peak) peak = inter;
                }
            }
        }
        return Dsp.linToDb(peak);
    }

    /** Integrated loudness in LUFS using the K-weighting filter. */
    static float integratedLufs(float[] buf, int frames, int ch, int sampleRate) {
        int block = Math.max(1, (int) (sampleRate * 0.4));
        int step = Math.max(1, (int) (sampleRate * 0.1));
        float[] shelf = Dsp.rbjHighShelf(sampleRate, 1681.97, 0.7071, 4f);
        float[] hp = Dsp.rbjHighPass(sampleRate, 38.13, 0.5003);
        float[] scratch = new float[block * ch];
        java.util.List<Float> blockLufs = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
        for (int start = 0; start + block <= frames; start += step) {
            System.arraycopy(buf, start * ch, scratch, 0, block * ch);
            BiquadFilter f = new BiquadFilter();
            f.setSections(new float[][]{shelf, hp}, ch);
            f.process(scratch, block, ch);
            double sum = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < block * ch; i++) {
                sum += (double) scratch[i] * scratch[i];
            }
            double mean = sum / (block * (double) ch);
            blockLufs.add((float) (-0.691 + 10 * Math.log10(Math.max(1e-12, mean))));
        }
        if (blockLufs.isEmpty()) return -70f;
        double gated = 0;
        int n = 0;
        for (float l : blockLufs) {
            if (l > -70f) {
                gated += Math.pow(10, (l + 0.691) / 10.0);
                n++;
            }
        }
        if (n == 0) return -70f;
        double ungated = -0.691 + 10 * Math.log10(gated / n);
        double rel = ungated - 10.0;
        gated = 0;
        n = 0;
        for (float l : blockLufs) {
            if (l > -70f && l > rel) {
                gated += Math.pow(10, (l + 0.691) / 10.0);
                n++;
            }
        }
        if (n == 0) return (float) ungated;
        return (float) (-0.691 + 10 * Math.log10(gated / n));
    }

    /** Per-frame RMS levels in dBFS using 100 ms frames. */
    static float[] frameLevels(float[] buf, int frames, int ch, int sampleRate) {
        int size = Math.max(1, (int) (sampleRate * 0.1));
        int count = Math.max(1, frames / size);
        float[] out = new float[count];
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            int start = i * size;
            int end = Math.min(frames, start + size);
            double sum = 0;
            int n = 0;
            for (int f = start; f < end; f++) {
                for (int c = 0; c < ch; c++) {
                    double v = buf[f * ch + c];
                    sum += v * v;
                    n++;
                }
            }
            out[i] = (float) (10 * Math.log10(Math.max(1e-12, sum / Math.max(1, n))));
        }
        return out;
    }

    /** Difference between the loudest and quietest deciles, in dB. */
    static float contrastDb(float[] frameDb) {
        if (frameDb == null || frameDb.length < 4) return 0f;
        float[] sorted = frameDb.clone();
        java.util.Arrays.sort(sorted);
        int n = sorted.length;
        int tenth = Math.max(1, n / 10);
        double loud = 0;
        for (int i = n - tenth; i < n; i++) loud += sorted[i];
        double quiet = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < tenth; i++) quiet += sorted[i];
        loud /= tenth;
        quiet /= tenth;
        return (float) (loud - quiet);
    }

    /** Dynamic range in loudness units (95th minus 10th percentile). */
    static float dynamicRangeLu(float[] buf, int frames, int ch, int sampleRate) {
        float[] frameDb = frameLevels(buf, frames, ch, sampleRate);
        if (frameDb.length < 4) return 0f;
        float[] sorted = frameDb.clone();
        java.util.Arrays.sort(sorted);
        int n = sorted.length;
        int hi = Math.max(0, (int) (n * 0.95) - 1);
        int lo = Math.min(n - 1, (int) (n * 0.10));
        return sorted[hi] - sorted[lo];
    }
}
