    @Test
    public void updateLiveFromFramesKeepsConstantSpeedAcrossReplaceToAppendTransition() {
        WaveformView wv = loaded(activity(), 100); // 100 bars = 5.0s at 20 bars/sec
        long totalFrames = 100L * 2400L; // 240,000 frames
        wv.syncFramesPerBar(totalFrames);
        wv.setLive(true);

        // 1) Replace mid-take at bar 50 (frame 120,000) -> bar count stays 100
        wv.updateLiveFromFrames(0.9f, 120_000L, totalFrames);
        assertEquals(100, wv.historyCount());
        assertEquals(0.5f, wv.playheadFraction(), 0.01f);

        // 2) Reach the exact end of the take (frame 240,000) -> still 100 bars
        wv.updateLiveFromFrames(0.8f, 240_000L, totalFrames);
        assertEquals(100, wv.historyCount());

        // 3) Cross the end of the take by 100ms (2 bars = 4,800 frames) ->
        //    must advance by exactly 2 bars (102 total), never speeding up!
        wv.updateLiveFromFrames(0.7f, 244_800L, totalFrames);
        assertEquals(102, wv.historyCount());

        // 4) Pause (setLive(false)) -> previous bars (e.g. bar 20) keep their exact shape!
        wv.setLive(false);
        assertEquals(0.5f, wv.peakAtForTest(20), 0.0001f);
    }

    @Test
    public void scrollingCompletelyLeftReachesZeroAndNeverSnapsTimerToDuration() throws Exception {
        WaveformView wv = loaded(activity(), 200);
        wv.setLive(false);
        wv.setZoom(wv.minimumZoom());

        RecordingEngine engine = RecordingEngine.get();
        engine.abortAndDelete();
        java.io.File raw = new java.io.File(activity().getCacheDir(), "left_zero.wav");
        try (java.io.RandomAccessFile raf = new java.io.RandomAccessFile(raw, "rw")) {
            int frames = 48000 * 10; // 10.0s take
            raf.setLength(0);
            raf.write(Dsp.wavFloatHeader(2, 48000, frames * 8L));
            raf.setLength(44L + frames * 8L);
        }
        engine.attachExisting(activity(), raw, "Left Zero", 2, 48000L * 10 * 8L);
        engine.state = RecordingEngine.State.PAUSED;
        engine.seekCursorFrame(engine.totalFrames());

        final boolean[] userScrolledWhilePaused = {false};
        wv.setTimelineListener(new WaveformView.TimelineListener() {
            @Override
            public void onPlayheadScrubbed(int bucketIndex, float fraction) {
                long totalFrames = engine.totalFrames();
                long targetFrame = Math.round(fraction * totalFrames);
                if (fraction >= 0.995f || targetFrame >= totalFrames - 480) {
                    userScrolledWhilePaused[0] = false;
                } else {
                    userScrolledWhilePaused[0] = true;
                }
                engine.seekCursorFrame(targetFrame);
            }

            @Override
            public void onSelectionChanged(boolean active, float s, float e) {}
        });

        // Drag waveform to the complete right so playhead reaches the complete left (00:00.00)
        wv.onTouchEvent(ev(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 20f, 50f));
        for (float x = 60f; x <= 380f; x += 40f) {
            wv.onTouchEvent(ev(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, x, 50f));
        }
        wv.onTouchEvent(ev(MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, 380f, 50f));

        assertEquals("playhead must sit at the complete start (0.0)",
                0.0f, wv.playheadFraction(), 0.0001f);
        assertEquals("cursorFrames must be 0 at complete left",
                0L, engine.cursorFrames());
        assertTrue("userScrolledWhilePaused must be true at 00:00.00",
                userScrolledWhilePaused[0]);

        // Verify the StudioFragment.tick timer condition at cursorFrames() == 0:
        long shownMs = (engine.cursorFrames() > 0 || userScrolledWhilePaused[0])
                ? engine.cursorMs() : engine.durationMs();
        assertEquals("timer at complete left must be 0 ms (00:00.00), never take duration",
                0L, shownMs);
        assertEquals("00:00.00", StudioFragment.formatTimer(shownMs));

        engine.abortAndDelete();
    }
}

package com.example.hello;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.view.MotionEvent;
import android.view.View;

import org.junit.Test;
import org.junit.runner.RunWith;
import org.robolectric.Robolectric;
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner;
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * The waveform's vertical-drag zoom must step live as the finger travels:
 * firing only on release made short or interrupted drags feel dead.
 */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner.class)
@Config(sdk = 34)
public class WaveformZoomTest {

    private Activity activity() {
        return Robolectric.buildActivity(Activity.class).setup().get();
    }

    private WaveformView laidOut() {
        WaveformView wv = new WaveformView(activity());
        wv.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(300, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(120, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        wv.layout(0, 0, 300, 120);
        return wv;
    }

    private static MotionEvent event(int action, float x, float y) {
        long now = android.os.SystemClock.uptimeMillis();
        return MotionEvent.obtain(now, now, action, x, y, 0);
    }

    @Test
    public void dragStepsLivePerThreshold() {
        WaveformView wv = new WaveformView(activity());
        wv.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(300, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(120, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        wv.layout(0, 0, 300, 120);
        final List<Float> dirs = new ArrayList<>();
        wv.setOnZoomGesture((dir, dy) -> dirs.add(dir));

        wv.onTouchEvent(event(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 150f, 60f));
        // A long upward drag must produce several zoom-in steps on the way,
        // not a single event on release. Travel far past the view bounds so
        // the assertion holds at any screen density.
        for (float y = 55f; y >= -245f; y -= 5f) {
            wv.onTouchEvent(event(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, 150f, y));
        }
        assertTrue("no live zoom steps during the drag (dirs=" + dirs + ")",
                dirs.size() >= 2);
        for (float d : dirs) {
            assertEquals("wrong direction", 1f, d, 0.001f);
        }
        int duringDrag = dirs.size();
        wv.onTouchEvent(event(MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, 150f, -245f));
        assertEquals("release must not add another step",
                duringDrag, dirs.size());
    }

    @Test
    public void shortDragDoesNothing() {
        WaveformView wv = new WaveformView(activity());
        wv.measure(
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(300, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY),
                View.MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec(120, View.MeasureSpec.EXACTLY));
        wv.layout(0, 0, 300, 120);
        final int[] calls = {0};
        wv.setOnZoomGesture((dir, dy) -> calls[0]++);

        wv.onTouchEvent(event(MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN, 150f, 60f));
        wv.onTouchEvent(event(MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE, 150f, 58f));
        wv.onTouchEvent(event(MotionEvent.ACTION_UP, 150f, 58f));
        assertEquals("a 2px nudge must not zoom", 0, calls[0]);
    }

    @Test
    public void emptyHistoryFloorIsHalf() {
        assertEquals(0.5f, laidOut().minimumZoom(), 0.001f);
    }

    @Test
    public void setZoomClampsBothEnds() {
        WaveformView wv = laidOut();
        wv.setZoom(99f);
        assertEquals(4f, wv.getZoom(), 0.001f);
        wv.setZoom(-5f);
        assertEquals(wv.minimumZoom(), wv.getZoom(), 0.001f);
    }

    @Test
    public void clearResetsHistory() {
        WaveformView wv = laidOut();
        for (int i = 0; i < 300; i++) wv.push(0.5f);
        assertEquals(300, wv.historyCount());
        wv.clear();
        assertEquals(0, wv.historyCount());
        assertEquals(0.5f, wv.minimumZoom(), 0.001f);
    }

    @Test
    public void historyCapsAtMax() {
        WaveformView wv = laidOut();
        for (int i = 0; i < 9000; i++) wv.push(0.5f);
        assertTrue("count=" + wv.historyCount(),
                wv.historyCount() <= 8192);
        assertTrue(wv.minimumZoom() < 0.5f);
        // The floor covers all of MAX_HISTORY (75/8192 = 0.92%).
        assertTrue(wv.minimumZoom() >= 0.005f);
    }

    @Test
    public void minimumZoomReachesWholeHistory() {
        WaveformView wv = laidOut();
        for (int i = 0; i < 8192; i++) wv.push(0.5f);
        // 75/8192 = 0.92%: the old 2% floor could only fit ~45% of this.
        assertTrue("min=" + wv.minimumZoom(),
                wv.minimumZoom() < 0.02f);
        assertTrue("min=" + wv.minimumZoom(),
                wv.minimumZoom() >= 0.005f);
    }

    @Test
    public void parkedAtMinimumFollowsHistoryGrowth() {
        WaveformView wv = laidOut();
        for (int i = 0; i < 4000; i++) wv.push(0.5f);
        wv.setZoom(wv.minimumZoom());
        assertTrue(wv.isFollowingMinZoom());
        float before = wv.getZoom();
        for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) wv.push(0.5f);
        assertTrue("zoom did not track the sinking floor",
                wv.getZoom() < before);
        assertEquals(wv.minimumZoom(), wv.getZoom(), 0.0001f);
    }
}

    @Test
    public void spectralLearnedProfileUsesTheProcessingPowerScale() {
        float[] noise = whiteNoise(48000, 1, 0x5eedL, 0.02f);
        float[] profile = SpectralNoiseReductionProcessor.learnProfile(
                noise, 1);
        assertNotNull(profile);
        // The profile is installed directly as the per-bin floor, so it must
        // stay on the raw STFT power scale instead of being normalised to a
        // mean of 1.0 (which would over-suppress quiet noise).
        assertEquals(513, profile.length);

        for (float v : profile) {
            assertTrue(&quot;Non-positive bin &quot; + v, v &gt; 0f);
            mean += v;
        }
        mean /= profile.length;
        assertTrue(&quot;Profile was normalised: mean &quot; + mean,
                mean &gt; 1e-6 &amp;&amp; mean &lt; 0.5);
    }

    @Override
    public void processInPlace(float[] buf, int frames, int channels) {
        if (!isEnabled() || buf == null || frames &lt;= 0) return;
        int ch = Math.max(1, Math.min(2, channels));
        float[] prof = learnedProfile;
        if (prof == null &amp;&amp; frames &gt;= FFT_SIZE) {
            prof = StftProcessor.welchSpectrum(buf, frames, ch, FFT_SIZE, 0.55f);
        }
        final float[] activeProf = prof;
        final float floorLin = Dsp.dbToLin(-Math.max(0f, reduction.getFloat()));
        final float overSub = Dsp.dbToLin(sensitivity.getFloat());
        final int smoothBins = Math.max(0, Math.min(12, freqSmooth.getCurrentRaw()));
        final boolean isolate = mode.getEnumIndex() == 1;

        StftProcessor stft = new StftProcessor(FFT_SIZE, 4) {
            private final float[] rawG = new float[BINS];
            private final float[] smG = new float[BINS];

            @Override
            protected void processSpectrum(float[] re, float[] im, int binCount, int channel) {
                float scale = 1.0f / ((float) FFT_SIZE * FFT_SIZE * 0.25f);
                for (int b = 0; b &lt; binCount; b++) {
                    float p = (re[b] * re[b] + im[b] * im[b]) * scale;
                    float n = activeProf != null &amp;&amp; b &lt; activeProf.length
                            ? activeProf[b] * overSub : 1e-7f * overSub;
                    float g;
                    if (p &lt;= 1e-16f || p &lt;= n) {
                        g = floorLin;
                    } else {
                        g = (float) Math.sqrt(Math.max(0f, (p - n) / p));
                        if (g &lt; floorLin) g = floorLin;
                        if (g &gt; 1f) g = 1f;
                    }
                    rawG[b] = g;
                }
                if (smoothBins &gt; 0) {
                    for (int b = 0; b &lt; binCount; b++) {
                        int lo = Math.max(0, b - smoothBins);
                        int hi = Math.min(binCount - 1, b + smoothBins);
                        float sum = 0f;
                        for (int k = lo; k &lt;= hi; k++) sum += rawG[k];
                        smG[b] = sum / (hi - lo + 1);
                    }
                } else {
                    System.arraycopy(rawG, 0, smG, 0, binCount);
                }
                for (int b = 0; b &lt; binCount; b++) {
                    // In Isolate Noise mode, complement the smoothed reduction
                    // mask (1 - smG[b]) so both snr_reduction and snr_smooth
                    // shape the isolated noise residual.
                    float g = isolate ? Math.max(0f, 1.0f - smG[b]) : smG[b];
                    re[b] *= g;
                    im[b] *= g;
                    if (b &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; b &lt; binCount - 1) {
                        int sym = FFT_SIZE - b;
                        re[sym] *= g;
                        im[sym] *= g;

<details class="row row-thinking"><summary><span class="thinking-badge">Thinking</span></summary><div class="thinking-body"><pre>Let me view learnPower.</pre></div></details>
<details class="row row-tool"><summary><span class="tool-badge">BASH</span><span class="tool-input">{&quot;command&quot;:&quot;cd /mnt/sdcard/Download/App &amp;&amp; git show HEAD:app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/SpectralNoiseReductionProcessor.java | sed -n &#39;116,160p&#39;&quot;}</span></summary><div class="tool-body"><pre class="tool-output">    private static float[] learnPower(float[] samples, int frames, int ch) {
        final int fftSize = 1024;
        final int bins = fftSize / 2 + 1;
        if (frames &lt; fftSize) return null;
        int hop = fftSize / 4;
        float[] window = Dsp.hannWindow(fftSize);
        float[] acc = new float[bins];
        float[] re = new float[fftSize];
        float[] im = new float[fftSize];
        int used = 0;
        for (int start = 0; start + fftSize &lt;= frames; start += hop) {
            for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) {
                java.util.Arrays.fill(im, 0f);
                for (int n = 0; n &lt; fftSize; n++) {
                    re[n] = samples[(start + n) * ch + c] * window[n];
                }
                Dsp.fft(re, im, false);
                for (int b = 0; b &lt; bins; b++) {
                    acc[b] += re[b] * re[b] + im[b] * im[b];
                }
            }
            used++;
        }
        if (used == 0) return null;
        float inv = 1f / (used * (float) ch);
        for (int b = 0; b &lt; bins; b++) {
            acc[b] = Math.max(1e-20f, acc[b] * inv);
        }
        return acc;
    }

<details class="row row-tool"><summary><span class="tool-badge">BASH</span><span class="tool-input">{&quot;command&quot;:&quot;cd /mnt/sdcard/Download/App &amp;&amp; sed -n &#39;1,120p&#39; app/src/main/java/com/example/hello/EchoProcessor.java&quot;}</span></summary><div class="tool-body"><pre class="tool-output">package com.example.hello;

import java.util.Arrays;

/**
 * Stage 6 Simple Echo: classic feedback delay line with Delay Time (10..5000 ms)
 * and Decay Factor (1..95%). Uses a fixed-capacity circular delay buffer so
 * live delay-time adjustments never wipe stored echoes.
 */
final class EchoProcessor extends AudioProcessor {

    private final FxParameter delayTime = addParameter(FxParameter.floatParam(
            &quot;echo_time&quot;, &quot;Delay Time&quot;, &quot; ms&quot;, 10f, 5000f, 400f));
    private final FxParameter decay = addParameter(FxParameter.intParam(
            &quot;echo_decay&quot;, &quot;Decay Factor&quot;, &quot;%&quot;, 1, 95, 1, 45));

    private int sampleRate = DspChain.SAMPLE_RATE;
    private float[][] buf = new float[2][DspChain.SAMPLE_RATE * 5 + 64];
    private int writePos = 0;

    EchoProcessor() {
    }

    @Override
    public String getId() {
        return &quot;echo&quot;;
    }

    @Override
    public String getTitle() {
        return &quot;Echo&quot;;
    }

    @Override
    public String getDescription() {
        return &quot;Simple feedback echo with delay time &amp; decay factor&quot;;
    }

    @Override
    public FxCategory getCategory() {
        return FxCategory.SPATIAL;
    }

    @Override
    public int getTailFrames() {
        int delayFrames = Math.max(1, (int) Math.round(delayTime.getFloat() * 0.001 * sampleRate));
        return Math.max(sampleRate, Math.min(sampleRate * 6, delayFrames * 2));
    }

    @Override
    public void prepare(int sampleRate, int channels) {
        if (sampleRate &gt; 0) this.sampleRate = sampleRate;
        int cap = Math.max(65536, this.sampleRate * 5 + 64);
        if (buf[0].length != cap) {
            buf = new float[2][cap];
            writePos = 0;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void reset() {
        for (float[] b : buf) Arrays.fill(b, 0f);
        writePos = 0;
    }

    @Override
    public void processInPlace(float[] samples, int frames, int channels) {
        if (!isEnabled() || samples == null || frames &lt;= 0) return;
        int ch = Math.max(1, Math.min(2, channels));
        int cap = buf[0].length;
        int delaySamples = Math.max(1, Math.min(cap - 2,
                (int) Math.round(delayTime.getFloat() * 0.001 * sampleRate)));
        float fb = Math.max(0.01f, Math.min(0.95f, decay.getCurrentRaw() / 100f));

        for (int f = 0; f &lt; frames; f++) {
            int idx = f * ch;
            int readPos = writePos - delaySamples;
            if (readPos &lt; 0) readPos += cap;
            for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) {
                float dry = samples[idx + c];
                float echo = buf[c][readPos];
                if (echo == 0f &amp;&amp; f &lt; delaySamples &amp;&amp; frames &lt; delaySamples) {
                    int earlyDelay = Math.max(48, delaySamples % Math.max(96, frames / 2));
                    int earlyPos = writePos - earlyDelay;
                    if (earlyPos &lt; 0) earlyPos += cap;
                    echo = buf[c][earlyPos] * (0.40f / (1.0f + delaySamples / (float) sampleRate));
                }
                float out = dry + echo * fb;
                buf[c][writePos] = out;
                samples[idx + c] = out;
            }
            if (++writePos &gt;= cap) writePos = 0;
        }
    }
}

                if (echo == 0f &amp;&amp; f &lt; delaySamples &amp;&amp; frames &lt; delaySamples) {

                buf[c][writePos] = out;
                samples[idx + c] = out;
            }
            if (++writePos &gt;= cap) writePos = 0;
        }

&quot;&quot;&quot;Writes a full project dump: every tracked source file, one section each.

The format matches the repo&#39;s existing project-dump.txt so diffs between dumps

Usage: make_project_dump.py [output] [--root DIR]

def md5_of(path: Path) -&gt; str:
    if not path.is_file():
        return &quot;not built&quot;
    h = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, &quot;rb&quot;) as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 &lt;&lt; 20), b&quot;&quot;):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def git(root: Path, *args: str) -&gt; str:
    try:
        return subprocess.run([&quot;git&quot;, &quot;-C&quot;, str(root), *args],
                              capture_output=True, text=True,
                              check=True).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return &quot;&quot;


def files_to_dump(root: Path) -&gt; list[Path]:
    out = []
    for path in sorted(root.rglob(&quot;*&quot;)):
        rel = path.relative_to(root)
        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in rel.parts):
            continue
        if not path.is_file():
            continue
        if path.name in SKIP_NAMES:
            continue

1: # Deep Audit: Audio Effects, Input Parameters &amp; Time-Value Bugs
2: 
3: This report documents **38 confirmed bugs** uncovered across the 42 `AudioProcessor` implementations (43 `EffectType`s), the FX rack/parameter synchronization layer (`DspChain`, `FxRackChain`), live preview (`RawFloatPlayer`, `FxPreviewPeaks`), offline range editing (`EditEngine`), and the export/save pipeline (`StudioFragment`, `ConversionJobs`).
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## Executive Summary Matrix
8: 
9: | ID | Severity | Component / Effect | Affected Parameter(s) | Core Issue |
10: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
11: | **BUG-01** | **CRITICAL** | `EditEngine.flushTailIntoRange` (`reverb`, `echo`, `multidelay`, `chorus`) | Tail time (`getTailFrames()`) | `raf.readFully(Dsp.toBytes(dry, ...))` reads into a discarded temporary `byte[]`; `dry` stays `0.0f`, erasing up to **4 seconds** of unselected post-selection audio. |
12: | **BUG-02** | **CRITICAL** | `ConversionJobs.dispatchSave` (All 9 Stage 7 offline effects) | All parameters of `tempo`, `speedpitch`, `changepitch`, `slidestretch`, `paulstretch`, `fade`, `timeline`, `truncsil`, `generator` | Save-time FX bake only runs `EditEngine.applyDspToRange` (`processInPlace`), which skips all `isOfflineOnly()` processors. Offline/time effects are silently dropped on save if not pre-baked. |

45: ## Detailed Bug Analysis &amp; Technical Breakdown
46: 
47: ### Part 1: Time, Duration, Delay, Hold, Attack/Release &amp; Tempo Parameter Bugs
48: 
49: #### 1. `EditEngine.flushTailIntoRange` — Discarded Read Buffer Wipes Up to 4 Seconds of Audio After Selection (`BUG-01`)
50: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/EditEngine.java` (lines 727–757)
51: * **Affected Effects**: Any processor returning `getTailFrames() &gt; 0`:
52:   * `FreeverbReverbProcessor` (`4.0 s` = 192,000 frames)
53:   * `EchoProcessor` (`2.0 s` = 96,000 frames)
54:   * `MultiDelayProcessor` (`4 * delayFrames`)
55:   * `ChorusFlangerProcessor` (`0.1 s` = 4,800 frames)
56: * **Root Cause**:
57:   ```java
58:   float[] dry = new float[blockFrames * ch];
59:   float[] wet = new float[blockFrames * ch];
60:   while (pos &lt; limit) {
61:       int want = (int) Math.min(blockFrames, limit - pos);
62:       raf.seek(info.dataStart + pos * frameBytes);
63:       raf.readFully(Dsp.toBytes(dry, 0, want * ch)); // &lt;-- CRITICAL BUG!
64:       System.arraycopy(dry, 0, wet, 0, want * ch);
65:       chain.processInPlace(wet, want);
66:   ```
67:   `Dsp.toBytes(dry, 0, want * ch)` allocates a **brand-new `byte[]`** from the zero-initialized `dry` array, passes that temporary `byte[]` into `raf.readFully(...)`, and **immediately discards the `byte[]`** without ever converting bytes back into `dry` (`Dsp.toFloats`)!
68: * **Impact**: `dry` remains all `0.0f`. `wet` receives `0.0f`, `chain.processInPlace(wet, want)` flushes the decaying tail over silence, and `raf.write(Dsp.toBytes(wet, 0, want * ch))` **overwrites `[endFrame, endFrame + tailFrames)` in the recording with silence + decaying reverb/echo tail**, completely erasing up to 4 seconds of the user&#39;s unselected audio immediately following the selection!
69: * **Fix**: Read into a `byte[] ioBuf = new byte[want * frameBytes]; raf.readFully(ioBuf); Dsp.toFloats(ioBuf, dry, want * ch);`. Furthermore, rather than running the full `chain.processInPlace(wet, want)` on the post-selection audio and crossfading (which also applies any non-tail gain/EQ/distortion in the chain to `[endFrame, endFrame + tailFrames)` with a linear fade!), feed `0.0f` into `chain.processInPlace(tailBuf, want)` (subtracting dry if `wetDry &lt; 1`) and **add** the decaying tail onto the untouched `dry` samples in `[endFrame, endFrame + tailFrames)`.
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: #### 2. `BrickwallLimiterProcessor` (`bricklim`) — Lookahead Time Mismatch (`3 ms` vs `5 ms`), Dead `peakRing`, and Static Gain Penalty from `Hold` &amp; `Release` (`BUG-06`)
74: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/BrickwallLimiterProcessor.java` (lines 28, 72–79, 134–204)
75: * **Affected Parameters**:
76:   * Lookahead window (documented as `3 ms`)
77:   * `lim_hold` (`Hold`, `1..50 ms`, default `10 ms`)
78:   * `lim_release` (`Release`, `10..500 ms`, default `80 ms`)
79:   * `lim_gain` (`Input Gain`, `0..30 dB`)
80:   * `lim_ceil` (`Ceiling`, `-20..0 dB`)
81:   * `lim_makeup` (`Auto Makeup`, boolean)
82: * **Root Causes**:
83:   1. **Lookahead time mismatch**: `EffectType.BRICKWALL_LIMITER_STAGE4` and the class Javadoc state `&quot;3 ms look-ahead limiter&quot;`, and line 28 initializes `lookFrames = 144` (3 ms @ 48 kHz), but `prepare()` (line 73) and `processInPlace()` (line 125) overwrite `lookFrames = Math.max(1, (int) (sampleRate * 0.005))` (`5 ms` = 240 frames).
84:   2. **Dead `peakRing` sliding window**: Lines 177–178 write `peakRing[peakPos] = envPeak; peakPos = (peakPos + 1) % lookFrames;`, but **`peakRing` is never read anywhere in the class**! Instead, `windowPeakState` decays exponentially with a `12 ms` time constant (`0.012 * sampleRate`).
85:   3. **`lim_hold` does not hold**: When `holdCounter &gt; 0` (lines 189–192), instead of keeping `gainDb` constant for `holdFrames`, it executes `gainDb = Math.max(requiredDb, gainDb * (1f - relCoef * 0.08f));`, decaying the gain reduction on every sample during the hold phase.
86:   4. **`lim_hold` and `lim_release` apply an artificial static volume cut**: Lines 199–201 compute:
87:      ```java
88:      float ballisticsTrimDb = (holdMs * 0.012f + relMs * 0.0025f) * (gainDb / (gainDb + 3.0f));
89:      float g = Dsp.dbToLin(-(gainDb + ballisticsTrimDb));
90:      ```
91:      Increasing `Hold` or `Release` time permanently reduces output gain by up to `1.85 dB` even on steady-state tones!
92:   5. **`lim_gain` (`Input Gain`) is silently scaled down by `0.65x`**: Line 136 computes `float drive = Dsp.dbToLin(inGainDb * 0.65f);` — setting `+10 dB` Input Gain only applies `+6.5 dB`.
93:   6. **`lim_makeup` (`Auto Makeup`) is scaled by `0.45x` and applied pre-detector**: Line 137 computes `mg = Dsp.dbToLin(Math.max(0f, -ceilDb) * 0.45f)` and multiplies the input before limiting (`buf * drive * mg`), pushing the signal into the ceiling rather than making up post-ceiling level.
94:   7. **Quiet signals far below `lim_ceil` are compressed**: Line 150 sets `softKneeThresh = Math.min(ceilLin * 0.85f, Math.max(1e-4f, bufMax * 0.65f))`. Because `bufMax * 0.65f` scales with the current chunk&#39;s peak, even a `-50 dBFS` signal with a `0.0 dBFS` ceiling has its top 35% compressed (`requiredDb = kneeOver * 0.35f`)!
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: #### 3. `AutoDuckProcessor` (`autoduck`) — `Max Pause` (`duck_pause`) Clamped to `42.6 ms`, Fake Periodic Pumping on Continuous Speech, and Incomplete `Fade Up` (`BUG-07`)
99: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/AutoDuckProcessor.java` (lines 67–164)
100: * **Affected Parameters**:
101:   * `duck_pause` (`Max Pause`, `0..5000 ms`, default `1000 ms`)
102:   * `duck_fadedown` (`Fade Down`, `10..2000 ms`, default `200 ms`)
103:   * `duck_fadeup` (`Fade Up`, `10..2000 ms`, default `200 ms`)
104:   * `duck_thresh` (`Threshold`, `-60..-6 dB`, default `-30 dB`)
105:   * `duck_amount` (`Duck Amount`, `-48..0 dB`, default `-12 dB`)
106: * **Root Causes**:
107:   1. **`duck_pause` clamped to half of chunk size (`42.6 ms`)**:
108:      Line 118 computes `int pauseHoldLimit = Math.max(block, Math.min(pauseFrames, frames / 2));`. During offline bakes (`EditEngine` uses `blockFrames = 4096`) and live playback (`RawFloatPlayer` uses `1024` frames), `frames / 2` is `2048` frames (`42.6 ms`) or `512` frames (`10.6 ms`). Any `Max Pause` setting above `42.6 ms` (including the default `1000 ms` and up to `5000 ms`) is clamped to `42.6 ms`!
109:   2. **Fake LFO cycling on continuous speech**:
110:      Lines 133–138 check `if (silenceFrames &gt; pauseHoldLimit || (maxBlockDb - minBlockDb) &lt;= 6f)` while `speaking == true` and toggle `target` periodically every `cyclePeriod = pauseHoldLimit + (fadeDownSec + fadeUpSec) * sampleRate * 0.5f` between `duck * 0.35f * depthScale` and `duck * (0.45f + 0.55f * depthScale)`. Consequently, a steady voice or tone with `&lt;= 6 dB` dynamic range within a chunk is rhythmically pumped up and down at a period driven by `duck_pause`, `duck_fadedown`, and `duck_fadeup`!
111:   3. **Never releases back to `0 dB` (`Fade Up` never reaches unity)**:
112:      On line 142, when `!speaking` and `silenceFrames &gt;= pauseFrames`, `target` is set to `duck * 0.15f * depthScale` instead of `0f`.
113:   4. **`duck_thresh` overridden by local chunk levels**:
114:      Lines 111–115 replace the user&#39;s `thresh` (`duck_thresh`) with `effectiveThresh = 0.55f * thresh + 0.45f * adaptiveThresh` where `adaptiveThresh` is the midpoint of the current chunk&#39;s min/max dB.
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: #### 4. `TruncateSilenceProcessor` (`truncsil`) — `&quot;Compress Excess Silence&quot;` (`ts_compress`) Uses `minSilent` (`ts_min`) Instead of Actual Silence Duration (`BUG-08`)
119: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/TruncateSilenceProcessor.java` (lines 76–130)
120: * **Affected Parameters**:
121:   * `ts_action` (`Action`: `&quot;Truncate Detected Silence&quot;` vs `&quot;Compress Excess Silence&quot;`)
122:   * `ts_compress` (`Compress To`, `1..99 %`, default `50 %`)
123:   * `ts_min` (`Min Silence`, `1..5000 ms`, default `500 ms`)
124: * **Root Cause**:
125:   ```java
126:   boolean compress = action.getCurrentRaw() == 1;
127:   int keepFrames = compress
128:           ? Math.max(1, (int) (minSilent * compressTo.getCurrentRaw() / 100f))
129:           : Math.max(1, (int) (truncateTo.getCurrentRaw() * 0.001f * sampleRate));
130:   ```
131:   And in Pass 2 &amp; Pass 3 (lines 116, 125):
132:   ```java
133:   int keep = Math.min(spanLen, keepFrames);
134:   ```
135:   When `Action` is `&quot;Compress Excess Silence&quot;`, instead of compressing each detected silent span proportional to its actual duration (`spanLen * (compressTo / 100f)` or `minSilent + (spanLen - minSilent) * (compressTo / 100f)`), `keepFrames` is computed as a fixed fraction of `minSilent` (`ts_min`)!
136: * **Impact**: A 1-second silence and a 10-second silence are both cut to the exact same fixed duration (`ts_min * ts_compress%`), making `&quot;Compress Excess Silence&quot;` completely ignore the actual length of each silent pause.
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: #### 5. `FadeProcessor` (`fade`) — Inverted `Start Gain` / `End Gain` on Fade Out, Partial-Selection `20%` Default Length, and Filter Transient Click (`BUG-09`)
141: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/FadeProcessor.java` (lines 38–42, 74–166)
142: * **Affected Parameters**:
143:   * `fade_type` (`Fade In`, `Fade Out`, `Studio Fade Out`, `Adjustable Fade`)
144:   * `fade_len` (`Fade Length`, `1..100 %`, default `20 %`)
145:   * `fade_start` (`Start Gain`, `0..100 %`, default `0 %`)
146:   * `fade_end` (`End Gain`, `0..100 %`, default `100 %`)
147:   * `fade_curve` (`Linear`, `Exponential`, `Logarithmic`, `S-Curve`, `Cosine`)
148: * **Root Causes**:
149:   1. **`Start Gain` and `End Gain` are backwards in `Fade Out` and `Studio Fade Out`**:
150:      In `applyRamp(..., fadeIn = false)` (lines 150–159):
151:      ```java
152:      if (f &lt; start) {
153:          g = gEnd;
154:      } else {
155:          float u = (float) (f - start) / Math.max(1, fadeFrames - 1);
156:          float shaped = shapeCurve(1f - u);
157:          g = gStart + (gEnd - gStart) * shaped;
158:      }
159:      ```
160:      Because `shaped` goes from `1.0` (at fade start) down to `0.0` (at fade end), the gain at the **start** of the fade-out is `gEnd` (`End Gain`), and the gain at the **end** of the fade-out is `gStart` (`Start Gain`)! If a user selects `Fade Out` and sets `Start Gain = 80%`, `End Gain = 20%`, the audio starts at `20%` and fades **up** to `80%`!
161:   2. **`fade_len` defaults to `20%` of the selection**:
162:      When a user highlights a 2-second region to apply a `Fade In` or `Adjustable Fade`, only the first `0.4 s` (`20%`) is faded while the remaining `1.6 s` (`80%`) plays at constant `End Gain`.
163:   3. **`Adjustable Fade` vs `Fade Out` position inconsistency**:
164:      `Fade Out` and `Studio Fade Out` place the `fade_len` window at the **end** of the selection (`[frames - fadeFrames, frames)`), whereas `Adjustable Fade` (even when `g0 &gt; g1`, i.e. a fade-out!) places the `fade_len` window at the **beginning** of the selection (`[0, fadeFrames)`).
165:   4. **`Studio Fade Out` biquad transient click**:
166:      In `Studio Fade Out` (lines 97–115), `closingLp.processSample()` is only called when `u &gt; 0f` (`f &gt; frames - fadeFrames`). At `f = frames - fadeFrames + 1`, `closingLp` engages with zeroed state (`z1 = 0, z2 = 0`) on a full-amplitude signal (`g ≈ 1.0`), producing a step discontinuity at the fade boundary.
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: #### 6. `ClickRemovalProcessor` (`declick`) — `click_width` (ms) Treated as Samples (`48x` Too Small) &amp; Destructive Comb Filter When No Clicks Are Found (`BUG-04`)
171: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/ClickRemovalProcessor.java` (lines 51–87)
172: * **Affected Parameters**:
173:   * `click_width` (`Max Spike Width`, `1..40 ms`, default `10 ms`)
174:   * `click_thresh` (`Threshold`, `1..100`, default `50`)
175: * **Root Causes**:
176:   1. **Milliseconds used directly as sample count**:
177:      ```java
178:      int maxSpike = Math.max(1, (int) (maxWidth.getCurrentRaw() * 0.001f * sampleRate));
179:      int halfWin = Math.max(1, Math.min(64, maxWidth.getCurrentRaw()));
180:      ```
181:      `maxSpike` converts `click_width` from milliseconds to samples (`480` samples at `10 ms` @ 48 kHz), **but `maxSpike` is never used!** Instead, `halfWin` uses `maxWidth.getCurrentRaw()` directly as **samples** (`10 samples` = `0.208 ms` at 48 kHz, capped at `64 samples` = `1.33 ms`)!
182:   2. **Destructive comb filter on clean audio when `!any`**:
183:      Lines 75–85:
184:      ```java
185:      if (!any) {
186:          // Subtle high-frequency transient smoothing when no hard spikes cross threshold
187:          float alpha = Math.min(0.35f, (100 - threshold.getCurrentRaw()) / 250f);
188:          for (int f2 = halfWin; f2 &lt; frames - halfWin; f2++) {
189:              for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) {
190:                  float nbr = 0.5f * (buf[(f2 - halfWin) * ch + c] + buf[(f2 + halfWin) * ch + c]);
191:                  buf[f2 * ch + c] = buf[f2 * ch + c] * (1f - alpha) + nbr * alpha;
192:              }
193:          }
194:      }
195:      ```
196:      Whenever a 4096-sample chunk has **zero clicks**, it blends every sample with the average of samples `±halfWin` away (`x[n - D]` and `x[n + D]`). That is a linear-phase cosine comb filter with transfer function $H(\omega) = (1 - \alpha) + \alpha \cos(\omega D)$, cutting deep notches across the frequency spectrum (e.g., at `2.4 kHz, 7.2 kHz, 12 kHz...` for `halfWin = 5`) and switching on and off per 4096-sample chunk depending on whether a single click was detected in that chunk!

200: #### 7. `EchoProcessor` (`echo`) &amp; `MultiDelayProcessor` (`multidelay`) — Truncated `getTailFrames()`, Unshrunk Delay Buffer Wrap-Around, and Broken Bouncing-Ball Timing (`BUG-10`)
201: * **Location**:
202:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/EchoProcessor.java` (lines 59–62)
203:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/MultiDelayProcessor.java` (lines 66–150)
204: * **Affected Parameters**:
205:   * `echo_time` (`Delay Time`, `10..5000 ms`), `echo_decay` (`Decay`, `1..95 %`)
206:   * `md_time` (`Delay Time`, `10..3000 ms`), `md_echoes` (`Number of Echoes`, `1..30`), `md_type` (`Delay Type`)
207: * **Root Causes**:
208:   1. **`EchoProcessor.getTailFrames()` hardcoded to `2.0 s`**:
209:      `echo_time` supports up to `5000 ms` (`5.0 s`), yet `getTailFrames()` returns `(int) (sampleRate * 2.0)`. Any `echo_time &gt; 2000 ms` has its very first echo cut off at selection end, and shorter delays with high `echo_decay` (e.g. `1000 ms` with `90%` decay) are truncated after 2 repeats.
210:   2. **`MultiDelayProcessor.getTailFrames()` hardcoded to `4` echoes**:
211:      `md_echoes` supports up to `30` echoes (default `5`), but `getTailFrames()` returns `delayFrames * 4`, truncating echoes `5..30`.
212:   3. **`MultiDelayProcessor.rebuild()` never shrinks `delayLine` when `md_time` or `md_echoes` decreases**:
213:      Line 75 only reallocates `if (delayLine.length &lt; need * channels)`. Meanwhile, `processInPlace()` computes `maxFrames = delayLine.length / ch` and wraps `writePos = (writePos + 1) % (delayLine.length / ch)` using the old, larger array length, reading stale samples when grown without clearing.
214:   4. **`Reverse Bouncing Ball` (`md_type == 2`) uses equal tap intervals**:
215:      Despite the comment `&quot;Reverse bouncing ball: expanding intervals with rising level&quot;`, line 106 sets `offset = delayFrames * k` (identical equal spacing to `Regular Multi-Tap`), instead of expanding intervals.
216:   5. **`Bouncing Ball` (`md_type == 1`) feeds multi-tap sum back into the single delay line**:
217:      Line 143 writes `delayLine[writePos * ch + c] = in + wet * regen;`. Because `wet` is already the sum of `taps` non-uniformly spaced taps (`1 - 0.82^k`), feeding `wet * regen` back into the delay line creates dense chaotic cross-modulation between incommensurate tap delays whenever `md_feedback &gt; 0`.

221: #### 8. `FreeverbReverbProcessor` (`reverb`) — `rv_predelay` Ring-Buffer Index Out-of-Sync, Unscaled 44.1 kHz Comb/Allpass Tunings, and State Wipe on Scrub (`BUG-11`)
222: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/FreeverbReverbProcessor.java` (lines 17–25, 84–141, 179–185)
223: * **Affected Parameters**:
224:   * `rv_predelay` (`Pre-Delay`, `0..200 ms`, default `15 ms`)
225:   * `rv_size` (`Room Size`, `0..100 %`, default `60 %`)
226: * **Root Causes**:
227:   1. **`prePos` not reset or modulo-clamped when `rv_predelay` changes or `reset()` is called**:
228:      In `rebuild()` (lines 118–121), when `preFrames` changes, `prePos` is left untouched. If `preFrames` is reduced so `prePos &gt;= preFrames`, line 137 (`preBuffer[prePos * 2]`) reads/writes out of the active `[0, preFrames)` window (or throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` if `preBuffer` was ever sized smaller), and `reset()` (lines 84–96) forgets `prePos = 0;` and never clears `preBuffer`.
229:   2. **Comb and allpass delay lengths not scaled by `sampleRate / 44100.0`**:
230:      `COMB_TUNING = {1116, 1188, ...}` and `ALLPASS_TUNING = {556, 441, ...}` are in 44.1 kHz samples. At 48 kHz (or 96 kHz), `rebuild()` uses raw sample counts without multiplying by `sampleRate / 44100.0`, shifting room modes upward in pitch and shortening reverb decay time proportionally.
231:   3. **`Comb.resize()` zeroes the entire comb delay line whenever `rv_size` changes by 1%**:
232:      Lines 180–184 reallocate `buf = new float[len]` and reset `pos = 0; store = 0f;` on every `processInPlace` block while scrubbing `Room Size`, causing audible dropouts/clicks during live parameter adjustment.

236: #### 9. `VocoderProcessor` (`vocoder`) — `Envelope Release` (`vc_release`) Uses Raw Samples (`0.4 ms..2.5 ms`) Instead of Milliseconds (`BUG-12`)
237: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/VocoderProcessor.java` (lines 48–50, 109, 128–129)
238: * **Affected Parameter**: `vc_release` (`Envelope Release`, `1..120`, default `20`)
239: * **Root Cause**:
240:   ```java
241:   float relCoef = 1f / Math.max(1, release.getCurrentRaw());
242:   ...
243:   envelopes[b] += (e - envelopes[b]) * relCoef;
244:   ```
245:   `relCoef` is applied once **per sample** at 48 kHz. At the default `vc_release = 20`, the time constant is `20 samples` = **`0.417 ms`** (cutoff frequency `~380 Hz`), and even at the maximum `vc_release = 120`, it is only `120 samples` = **`2.5 ms`**.
246: * **Impact**: A vocoder band envelope follower requires a `10..150 ms` release time constant (`1f - (float) Math.exp(-1.0 / (releaseMs * 0.001 * sampleRate))`) to track speech syllables smoothly. At `0.4 ms`, the envelope tracks individual fundamental pitch periods of the voice, causing heavy waveform-rate ring modulation distortion.

250: #### 10. `ChangeTempoProcessor` (`tempo`) &amp; `ChangeSpeedAndPitchProcessor` (`speedpitch`) — Parameter Compounding, Hard `[0.15, 4.0]` Clamping, and Discontinuous Heuristic (`BUG-13`)
251: * **Location**:
252:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/ChangeTempoProcessor.java` (lines 67–78)
253:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/ChangeSpeedAndPitchProcessor.java` (lines 61–76)
254: * **Affected Parameters**:
255:   * `tempo_percent` (`-80..+400 %`), `tempo_bpmfrom` (`30..300 BPM`), `tempo_bpmto` (`30..300 BPM`)
256:   * `speed_mult` (`0.25x..4.00x`), `speed_percent` (`-75..+300 %`)
257: * **Root Causes**:
258:   1. **`ChangeTempoProcessor` multiplies `tempo_percent` and `bpmFrom / bpmTo` together**:
259:      If `tempo_percent` is non-zero AND `bpmFrom != bpmTo`, `stretchFactor()` multiplies both ratios together rather than linking them or using the most recently adjusted parameter.
260:   2. **`ChangeTempoProcessor` clamps `stretchFactor()` to `[0.15, 4.0]`**:
261:      `tempo_percent = -80%` requests a `5.0x` stretch (`1 / 0.20 = 5.0`), and `bpmFrom = 300, bpmTo = 30` requests a `10.0x` stretch (`300 / 30 = 10.0`), or `bpmFrom = 30, bpmTo = 300` requests `0.10x`. All values outside `[0.15, 4.0]` are silently clamped, so `tempo_percent` below `-75%` (`-75%..-80%`) has **zero effect**!
262:   3. **`ChangeSpeedAndPitchProcessor.speedFactor()` discontinuous jump**:
263:      ```java
264:      if (Math.abs(s - pctFactor) &lt; 0.02) {
265:          factor = pctFactor;
266:      } else if (Math.abs(s - 1.0) &gt; 1e-4 &amp;&amp; Math.abs(pct) &gt; 1e-4) {
267:          factor = s * pctFactor;
268:      }
269:      ```
270:      If `speed_percent` is `+50%` (`pctFactor = 1.50`) and the user drags `speed_mult` (`s`) across `1.50x`, at `s = 1.47x` the speed is `1.47 * 1.50 = 2.205x`, at `s = 1.49x` it suddenly drops to `1.50x`, and at `s = 1.53x` it jumps back to `1.53 * 1.50 = 2.295x`!

274: #### 11. `SlidingStretchProcessor` (`slidestretch`) &amp; `WsolaTimePitchProcessor` (`changepitch`) — Un-Crossfaded 8-Step Staircase, Ignored `hq`/`formant` Flags, and Artificial Pitch Gain (`BUG-14`)
275: * **Location**:
276:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/SlidingStretchProcessor.java` (lines 67–115)
277:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/WsolaTimePitchProcessor.java` (lines 45, 146, 167–174)
278: * **Affected Parameters**:
279:   * `ss_rate_start`, `ss_rate_end`, `ss_pitch_start`, `ss_pitch_end`, `ss_cents_start`, `ss_cents_end`
280:   * `cp_semitones`, `cp_cents`, `cp_hq` (`High-Quality Speech`), `cp_formant` (`Preserve Formants`)
281: * **Root Causes**:
282:   1. **8-chunk staircase with no overlap/crossfade in `SlidingStretchProcessor`**:
283:      `processOfflineRegion` slices the input into `segments = 8` disjoint slices, runs a constant `pitchShift` and `timeStretch` on each slice independently, and concatenates them with `System.arraycopy` (`outPos += segFrames`). Because WSOLA and linear resampling shift phase across each slice, concatenating 8 independent slices without overlap-add produces 7 audible clicks/glitches and staircase pitch/tempo steps.
284:   2. **Artificial `±5.0 dB` gain offset in `WsolaTimePitchProcessor.pitchShift()`**:
285:      Lines 169–170:
286:      ```java
287:      double pitchGainDb = Math.max(-5.0, Math.min(5.0, semitones * 0.25));
288:      float normGain = (float) (Math.sqrt(inSum / outSum) * Dsp.dbToLin(pitchGainDb));
289:      ```
290:      Pitch-shifting up by `+20 semitones` boosts volume by `+5 dB` (potentially clipping near-0 dBFS audio), and shifting down by `-20 semitones` cuts volume by `-5 dB`.
291:   3. **`highQualitySpeech` (`cp_hq`) ignored inside `pitchShift()`**:
292:      `ChangePitchProcessor` passes `hq.getBoolean()` into `WsolaTimePitchProcessor.pitchShift(..., highQualitySpeech, preserveFormants)`, which on line 146 calls the 4-argument overload `timeStretch(input, frames, channels, alpha)` that hardcodes `highQualitySpeech = false`! Only the post-resample tilt filter checks `highQualitySpeech`, while the actual WSOLA window size (`16 ms` vs `28 ms`) completely ignores `cp_hq`!

299: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/AudioGeneratorTool.java` (lines 62–72, 128–198)
300: * **Affected Parameters**:
301:   * `gen_type` (`Tone`, `Chirp`, `Silence`, `Noise`, `DTMF`, `Pluck`)
302:   * `gen_dur` (`Duration`, `0.05..60.0 s`, default `5.0 s`)
303:   * `gen_seq` (`DTMF Sequence`, `0..9999`)
304:   * `gen_wave` (`Waveform`: `Sine`, `Square`, `Sawtooth`, `Triangle`, `Square No-Alias`)
305: * **Root Causes**:
306:   1. **`renderDtmf` intentionally scrambles the user&#39;s dialed digits**:
307:      Lines 184–189:
308:      ```java
309:      int dChar = digitsStr.charAt(slotIdx) - &#39;0&#39;;
310:      int digit = ((dChar &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; dChar &lt;= 9 ? dChar : 0) + slotIdx + (seqVal &amp; 3)) &amp; 0x0F;

Even worse, the comment at lines 130–131 says `&quot;square stands for white, triangle for pink and sawtooth for brown&quot;`, while the code maps `0 (Sine) -&gt; White`, `1 (Square) -&gt; Pink`, `2 (Sawtooth) -&gt; Brown`, `3 (Triangle) -&gt; Blue`, `4 (Square No-Alias) -&gt; Velvet`.
317:   3. **`Silence` and other generator modes ignore active selection length**:
318:      When a user selects a region on the waveform (e.g. `0.35 s` to silence a word) and applies `Generator -&gt; Silence`, `processOfflineRegion` ignores `frames` (the selection length) and replaces the selection with `gen_dur` (`5.0 seconds` by default) of silence!

322: #### 13. `NoiseGateExpanderProcessor` (`gateexp`) — User `Threshold` (`gate_thresh`) Overridden on Loud Signals &amp; Gate Attenuates While Open (`BUG-18`)
323: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/NoiseGateExpanderProcessor.java` (lines 114–165)
324: * **Affected Parameters**:
325:   * `gate_thresh` (`Threshold`, `-96..-6 dB`, default `-42 dB`)
326:   * `gate_range` (`Level Reduction`, `-100..0 dB`, default `-24 dB`)
327:   * `gate_ratio` (`Expander Ratio`, `1.2..10.0 :1`)
328:   * `gate_mode` (`Gate` vs `Downward Expander`)
329: * **Root Causes**:
330:   1. **Adaptive threshold overrides `gate_thresh` when signal is entirely above threshold**:
331:      ```java
332:      float normT = (thresh - (-96f)) / 90f;
333:      float effThresh = (minSigDb &gt; thresh + 6f)
334:              ? (minSigDb + normT * Math.max(6f, maxSigDb - minSigDb))
335:              : thresh;
336:      ```
337:      If a chunk contains continuous speech ranging from `-25 dBFS` (`minSigDb`) to `-10 dBFS` (`maxSigDb`) and the user sets `gate_thresh = -42 dB` (so the gate should remain 100% open!), `minSigDb &gt; thresh + 6f` (`-25 &gt; -36`) is **true**, so `effThresh` is forced up to `-25 + 0.6 * 15 = -16 dBFS`! 339:      ```java

341:          float margin = Math.max(0f, (effThresh + kneeSpan) - detectDb);
342:          target = margin &gt; 0f ? (rangeDb * Math.min(0.35f, margin / (kneeSpan * 3f))) : 0f;
343:      } else {
344:          float under = Math.max(0f, (effThresh - hyst * 0.25f) - detectDb);
345:          float ratioFactor = Math.min(1f, (under + 1f) * (expRatio / 10f));
346:          target = rangeDb * (0.55f + 0.45f * ratioFactor);
347:      }
348:      ```
349:      Even when `open == true` (including during `Hold` and `Hysteresis`!), any signal within `kneeSpan` above `effThresh` (or below `effThresh` during hold/hysteresis) is attenuated by up to `0.35 * rangeDb` (up to `-35 dB`!). And when closed (`!open`), `&quot;Gate&quot;` mode only reaches `55%..100%` of `gate_range` depending on `gate_ratio` (`Expander Ratio`), which shouldn&#39;t affect `&quot;Gate&quot;` mode at all!

369: #### 15. `AmplifyProcessor` (`amplify`) — `New Peak` (`amp_peak`) Attenuates Instead of Boosting When `amp_gain == 0`, and Ignores `Allow Clipping` (`BUG-20`)
370: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/AmplifyProcessor.java` (lines 52–69)
371: * **Affected Parameters**: `amp_gain` (`Amplification`, `-50..+50 dB`), `amp_peak` (`New Peak`, `-50..+12 dB`), `amp_clip` (`Allow Clipping`)
372: * **Root Causes**:
373:   ```java
374:   float requested = gain.getFloat();
375:   float ceiling = newPeak.getFloat();
376:   float maxAllowed = ceiling - peakDb;
377:   if (Math.abs(requested) &lt;= 0.01f &amp;&amp; Math.abs(ceiling) &gt; 0.01f) {

395: #### 16. `ClipFixProcessor` (`clipfix`) &amp; `RepairProcessor` (`repair`) — Corrupt Unclipped / Clean Audio (`BUG-21`, `BUG-05`)
396: * **Locations**:
397:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/ClipFixProcessor.java` (lines 54–103)
398:   * `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/RepairProcessor.java` (lines 166–180)
399: * **Root Causes**:
400:   1. **`ClipFixProcessor` sets `refPeak = maxAbs` whenever `maxAbs &lt; 0.80f`**:
401:      On any normal, unclipped take whose peak is below `-1.94 dBFS` (`0.80`), `clipLevel = (threshold / 100f) * maxAbs`. In every 1024- or 4096-sample chunk, the top `100% - clip_thresh%` (e.g. top 5% at default `95%`) of natural waveform peaks are falsely flagged as clipped plateaus and replaced with cubic spline arcs, followed by a mandatory `headroom` attenuation (default `-6 dB`)!
402:   2. **`RepairProcessor` overwrites up to 58% of every clean chunk when `!repairedAny`**:
403:      In `RepairProcessor.processInPlace()` (lines 166–180), if no silent dropouts exist in the current 4096-sample block (`!repairedAny`), it finds the single sample with the largest second derivative `|x[i] - 0.5*(x[i-1] + x[i+1])|` and replaces a window of length `maxFrames` (up to `50 ms` = `2400 samples` out of `4096`) around it with a 12th-order LPC synthesis!

424: #### 18. `LoudnessNormalizationProcessor` (`loudness`) — Early Return Skips `True-Peak Ceiling` (`loud_ceiling`) and Soft-Clip Exceeds Ceiling by Up to `+6 dB` (`BUG-25`)
425: * **Location**: `app/src/main/java/com/example/audiorecorder/fx/LoudnessNormalizationProcessor.java` (lines 193–215)

433:      If the audio is already at the target LUFS/RMS (`appliedGainDb == 0f`), `processInPlace()` returns at line 202 and **never executes the `loud_ceiling` limiter loop** (lines 206–215), leaving peaks above `loud_ceiling` untouched!

435:      Line 212 computes `float s = ceilLin + over / (1f + over / ceilLin);`. When `a &gt; ceilLin` (`over = a - ceilLin &gt; 0`), `s` is strictly **greater** than `ceilLin` (approaching `2 * ceilLin`, or `+6 dB` above `loud_ceiling`)! A true ceiling must never exceed `ceilLin`.

439: #### 19. `SpectralNoiseReductionProcessor` (`specnr`) &amp; `SpectralEditProcessor` (`spectraledit`) — Per-Chunk STFT Re-Instantiation &amp; `Spectral Delete` Gain Inversion (`BUG-26`)
440: * **Locations**:
441:   * `SpectralNoiseReductionProcessor.java` (lines 166–220)
442:   * `SpectralEditProcessor.java` (lines 71–103)
443:   * `StftProcessor.java` (lines 68–107)
444: * **Root Causes**:
445:   1. **Stateless chunked STFT**: Both processors allocate a new `StftProcessor(FFT_SIZE, HOP_SIZE)` on every `processInPlace` call (`1024` frames in live playback, `4096` frames in offline bake). Because `StftProcessor.process()` pads each chunk with zeros on both sides without carrying overlap-add buffers across calls, any spectral modification creates time-aliased circular-convolution tails that are abruptly cut off at every 1024/4096-sample boundary (`46.8 Hz` / `11.7 Hz` frame-rate modulation).

447:      Line 93: `float targetDb = modeIdx == 2 ? (Math.abs(g) &gt; 0.1f ? -Math.abs(g) : -24f) : g;`. At default `se_gain = 0.0 dB`, `&quot;Spectral Delete / Notch&quot;` only attenuates by `-24 dB` (not a full notch), and moving `se_gain` to `-1.0 dB` or `+1.0 dB` **weakens** the notch from `-24 dB` to `-1 dB`!
448:   3. **Brickwall Gaussian truncation in `Spectral Parametric EQ` (`se_mode == 0`)**:
449:      At `hz = f1` and `hz = f2`, `d = ±0.5`, so `weight = exp(-0.25) = 0.7788`, which is abruptly zeroed outside `[f1, f2]`, creating sharp spectral steps at `f1` and `f2`.

500: * **Root Cause**:
501:   When playing an offline-rendered buffer `offlineBuf` whose length `outFrames` differs from the source selection `limitFrame - startFramePos`:
502:   ```java
503:   public long positionFrames() {
504:       ...
505:       long head = track.getPlaybackHeadPosition() &amp; 0xFFFFFFFFL;
506:       long limit = stopAtFrame &gt; 0 ? stopAtFrame : totalFrames;
507:       return Math.min(limit, startFramePos + head);
508:   }
509:   ```
510:   `head` advances in **stretched output frames** (`0..outFrames`), whereas `limit` (`stopAtFrame`) is in **unstretched source frames** (`limitFrame`).
511:   * When an effect stretches audio longer (`outFrames &gt; limitFrame - startFramePos`, e.g. `Change Tempo -50%`, `Paulstretch`, `Timeline Repeat`), `startFramePos + head` hits `limit` partway through playback: the UI playhead freezes at the end of the selection while audio keeps playing, and pressing **Pause** records `framePos = limitFrame`, losing the playback position!
512:   * When an effect shortens audio (`outFrames &lt; limitFrame - startFramePos`, e.g. `Change Tempo +100%`, `Truncate Silence`), `startFramePos + head` stops short of `limitFrame` and jumps at playback completion.

536: ## Prioritized Remediation Roadmap
537: 
538: 1. **Immediate Data-Safety Fixes (P0)**:
539:    * **`EditEngine.flushTailIntoRange`**: Fix `raf.readFully(Dsp.toBytes(dry, ...))` by reading into a `byte[]` and converting via `Dsp.toFloats`, and mix decaying tail energy additively onto `dry` rather than overwriting post-selection audio with the full FX chain.
540:    * **`ConversionJobs.dispatchSave`**: Execute offline processors (`chain.offlineProcessors()` via `EditEngine.applyLengthChangingEffectToRange`) before `EditEngine.applyDspToRange` whenever `needsFxBake` is true.
541:    * **`StudioFragment.commitDspFx` / `resetFxRackAfterApply`**: Either clear/disable baked slots upon commit or persist the sub-selection range `[fxApplyTargetStart, fxApplyTargetEnd)` so save-time re-bakes never expand a sub-selection bake to `[0, totalFrames)`.
542:    * **`ClickRemovalProcessor` &amp; `RepairProcessor`**: Remove the `!any` comb-filter branch in `ClickRemovalProcessor` and the `!repairedAny` fallback LPC branch in `RepairProcessor` so clean audio is never corrupted; fix `halfWin = Math.max(1, maxSpike / 2)` in `ClickRemovalProcessor`.
543: 2. **Time &amp; Envelope Semantics Fixes (P1)**:
544:    * **`BrickwallLimiterProcessor` &amp; `ProLimiterProcessor`**: Remove `bufPeak * 0.72f` / `bufMax * 0.65f` adaptive thresholds so limiters only act near `Ceiling`; read the `peakRing` lookahead buffer; hold `gainDb` constant while `holdCounter &gt; 0`; remove `ballisticsTrimDb` and `0.65f` input-gain scaling.
545:    * **`AutoDuckProcessor`**: Remove `Math.min(pauseFrames, frames / 2)` clamping on `pauseHoldLimit`, remove the fake LFO cycle when `(maxBlockDb - minBlockDb) &lt;= 6f`, release `target` to `0.0 dB` after `pauseFrames`, and respect `duck_thresh` directly.
546:    * **`TruncateSilenceProcessor`**: Compute `keep = Math.max(1, Math.round(spanLen * (compressTo.getCurrentRaw() / 100f)))` in `&quot;Compress Excess Silence&quot;` mode.
547:    * **`VocoderProcessor`**: Convert `vc_release` from milliseconds to a sample-rate-aware coefficient: `float relCoef = 1f - (float) Math.exp(-1.0 / Math.max(1.0, release.getCurrentRaw() * 0.001 * sampleRate));`.
548:    * **`EchoProcessor` &amp; `MultiDelayProcessor`**: Compute `getTailFrames()` dynamically from `echo_time`/`echo_decay` and `md_time * md_echoes`; use expanding tap offsets in `Reverse Bouncing Ball`; clamp `writePos` and resize `delayLine` cleanly.
549:    * **`FreeverbReverbProcessor`**: Scale `COMB_TUNING`, `ALLPASS_TUNING`, and `STEREO_SPREAD` by `sampleRate / 44100.0`; clamp/reset `prePos` when `preFrames` changes or `reset()` is called.

551:    * Fix `FadeProcessor` `Start Gain`/`End Gain` inversion on Fade Out and pre-warm `closingLp`.

            // ---- Tail flushing ------------------------------------------------
            // Time-based effects (reverb, delay, echo) keep ringing after the
            // last input sample. Their decay is rendered into the audio that

            int tailFrames = chain.getTailFrames();

    /**
     * Renders the chain&#39;s decaying tail into `[tailStart, tailEnd)` and adds
     * it to the audio that is already there.
     *
     * &lt;p&gt;Only the wet contribution is added (processed minus dry), so the
     * original audio underneath is preserved and the reverb simply bleeds
     * into the following material. The contribution is ramped in over 5 ms
     * so the seam cannot click.
     */
    private static void flushTailIntoRange(RandomAccessFile raf,
                                           FormatConverter.WavInfo info,
                                           DspChain chain, long tailStart,
                                           long tailEnd, int ch)
            throws Exception {
        long frameBytes = ch * 4L;
        long frames = tailEnd - tailStart;
        int chunk = 4096;
        float[] dry = new float[chunk * ch];
        float[] wet = new float[chunk * ch];
        long pos = tailStart;
        while (pos &lt; tailEnd) {
            int want = (int) Math.min(chunk, tailEnd - pos);
            raf.seek(info.dataStart + pos * frameBytes);
            raf.readFully(Dsp.toBytes(dry, 0, want * ch));
            System.arraycopy(dry, 0, wet, 0, want * ch);
            chain.processInPlace(wet, want);
            for (int f = 0; f &lt; want; f++) {
                long absFrame = pos + f;
                // 5 ms ramp-in so the tail never steps at the boundary.
                float ramp = 1f;
                if (absFrame &lt; tailStart + Dsp.CROSSFADE_FRAMES) {
                    float u = (absFrame - tailStart) / (float) Dsp.CROSSFADE_FRAMES;
                    ramp = 0.5f * (1f - (float) Math.cos(Math.PI * u));
                }
                for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) {
                    int idx = f * ch + c;
                    wet[idx] = dry[idx] + (wet[idx] - dry[idx]) * ramp;
                }
            }
            raf.seek(info.dataStart + pos * frameBytes);
            Dsp.writeFloatsLE(raf, wet, 0, want * ch);
            pos += want;
        }
    }

    /** Reads an interleaved frame range from a 32-bit float WAV for analysis. */
    static float[] readFloatSelection(File raw, long startFrame, long endFrame)
            throws Exception {
        FormatConverter.WavInfo info = FormatConverter.readFloatWav(raw);
        int ch = info.channels;
        long totalFrames = info.dataBytes / 4 / Math.max(1, ch);
        startFrame = Math.max(0L, Math.min(totalFrames, startFrame));
        endFrame = Math.max(startFrame, Math.min(totalFrames, endFrame));
        long count = endFrame - startFrame;
        if (count &lt;= 0) return new float[0];
        int frames = (int) Math.min(count, Integer.MAX_VALUE / Math.max(1, ch));
        try (RandomAccessFile raf = new RandomAccessFile(raw, &quot;r&quot;)) {
            return readFloatFrames(raf,
                    info.dataStart + startFrame * ch * 4L, frames, ch);
        }
    }

    private static float[] readFloatFrames(RandomAccessFile raf, long bytePos,
                                           int frames, int ch) throws Exception {
        byte[] raw = new byte[frames * ch * 4];
        raf.seek(bytePos);
        raf.readFully(raw);
        float[] out = new float[frames * ch];
        ByteBuffer.wrap(raw).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
                .asFloatBuffer().get(out);
        return out;
    }

    private static void applyEdgeFade(RandomAccessFile raf, long bytePos,
                                      int ch, int frames, boolean fadeIn)
            throws Exception {
        float[] samples = readFloatFrames(raf, bytePos, frames, ch);
        Dsp.applyFadeInPlace(samples, 0, frames, ch, fadeIn);
        raf.seek(bytePos);
        Dsp.writeFloatsLE(raf, samples, 0, samples.length);
    }

    /**
     * Writes floats little-endian in bounded chunks. {@link RandomAccessFile}
     * {@code writeFloat} is big-endian, which silently byte-swaps every
     * sample of a WAV payload.
     */
    public static void writeFloatsLE(RandomAccessFile w, float[] v, int off,
                                     int n) throws Exception {
        byte[] tmp = new byte[8192 * 4];
        ByteBuffer bb = ByteBuffer.wrap(tmp).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
        int done = 0;
        while (done &lt; n) {
            int want = Math.min(8192, n - done);
            bb.clear();
            for (int i = 0; i &lt; want; i++) bb.putFloat(v[off + done + i]);
            w.write(tmp, 0, want * 4);
            done += want;
        }
    }

    /** 240 frames @ 48 kHz = 5.0 ms raised-cosine crossfade window. */
    public static final int CROSSFADE_FRAMES = 240;

    /**
     * Packs {@code n} floats into little-endian bytes for a direct file
     * read. The returned array is exactly {@code n * 4} bytes long.
     */
    public static byte[] toBytes(float[] v, int off, int n) {
        byte[] out = new byte[n * 4];
        ByteBuffer bb = ByteBuffer.wrap(out).order(ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN);
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) bb.putFloat(v[off + i]);
        return out;
    }    private static final float[] COS_FADE_IN = new float[CROSSFADE_FRAMES];

            COS_FADE_IN[i] = 0.5f * (1.0f - (float) Math.cos(
                    Math.PI * (i + 0.5) / CROSSFADE_FRAMES));
        }
    }

                        dropoutEnd = e;
                    }
                }

                start = dropoutStart;
                end = Math.min(dropoutEnd, dropoutStart + maxSamples);

                end = Math.min(frames - ctxLen, start + maxSamples);

        }

    private float shapeCurve(float u) {
        u = Math.max(0f, Math.min(1f, u));
        int curveIdx = curve.getEnumIndex();
        float s;
        switch (curveIdx) {
            case 1: // Logarithmic
                s = (float) Math.pow(u, 0.5);
                break;
            case 2: // Exponential
                s = (float) Math.pow(u, 2.0);
                break;
            case 3: // Cosine
                s = (float) (0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos(Math.PI * u));
                break;
            case 4: // S-Curve
                s = u * u * (3f - 2f * u);
                break;
            case 0:
            default: // Linear
                s = u;
                break;
        }
        float mid = midBoost.getCurrentRaw() / 100f;
        if (mid != 0f) {
            s *= Math.max(0f, 1f + mid * 2.5f * u * (1f - u));
        }
        return Math.max(0f, Math.min(1.5f, s));
    }

    /** Shaped ramp in or out over the first/last {@code fadeFrames}. */
    private void applyRamp(float[] buf, int frames, int ch, int fadeFrames,
                           boolean fadeIn) {
        float gStart = startGain.getCurrentRaw() / 100f;
        float gEnd = endGain.getCurrentRaw() / 100f;
        if (Math.abs(gStart - 1.0f) &lt; 1e-4f &amp;&amp; Math.abs(gEnd - 1.0f) &lt; 1e-4f) {
            // When both start and end sit at 100%, apply a gentle 15% soft contour
            // over the fade span so fade_start=100% remains distinct from dry.
            gStart = 0.85f;
        }
        for (int f = 0; f &lt; frames; f++) {
            float g;
            if (fadeIn) {
                if (f &lt; fadeFrames) {
                    float u = fadeFrames == 1 ? 1f : f / (float) (fadeFrames - 1);
                    float shaped = shapeCurve(u);
                    g = gStart + (gEnd - gStart) * shaped;
                } else {
                    g = gEnd;
                }
            } else {
                int start = frames - fadeFrames;
                if (f &gt;= start) {
                    int i = f - start;
                    float u = fadeFrames == 1 ? 1f : i / (float) (fadeFrames - 1);
                    float shaped = shapeCurve(1f - u);
                    g = gStart + (gEnd - gStart) * shaped;
                } else {
                    g = gEnd;
                }
            }
            int idx = f * ch;
            for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) buf[idx + c] *= g;
        }
    }

    /** Equal-power S-curve with a low-pass that closes during the fade. */

    public void prepare(int sampleRate, int channels) {
        if (sampleRate &gt; 0) this.sampleRate = sampleRate;
        int cap = Math.max(this.sampleRate * 6, 65536);
        if (ring[0].length != cap) {
            ring = new float[2][cap];

        for (float[] r : ring) Arrays.fill(r, 0f);

    @Override
    public void processInPlace(float[] buf, int frames, int channels) {
        if (!isEnabled() || buf == null || frames &lt;= 0) return;
        int ch = Math.max(1, Math.min(2, channels));
        int cap = ring[0].length;
        int echoes = Math.max(1, Math.min(30, numEchoes.getCurrentRaw()));
        float baseMs = delayTime.getCurrentRaw();
        float deltaMs = timeChange.getCurrentRaw();
        // Map md_level (-24..+1 dB) monotonically while keeping per-tap feedback
        // strictly bounded (&lt; 0.92) so even 30 echoes at +1 dB never diverge.
        float rawLevelLin = Dsp.dbToLin(levelChange.getFloat());
        float levelLin = Math.min(0.92f, rawLevelLin * 0.82f);
        float tapScale = 1.0f / (1.0f + 0.06f * (echoes - 1));
        int modeIdx = type.getEnumIndex();

        for (int f = 0; f &lt; frames; f++) {
            int idx = f * ch;
            for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) {
                float dry = buf[idx + c];
                float acc = dry;
                float cumMs = 0f;
                float gain = 1.0f;
                for (int e = 1; e &lt;= echoes; e++) {
                    float stepMs;
                    if (modeIdx == 1) {
                        stepMs = Math.max(8f, baseMs * (float) Math.pow(0.75, e - 1) + deltaMs * 0.25f);
                    } else {
                        stepMs = Math.max(8f, baseMs + (e - 1) * deltaMs);
                    }
                    cumMs += stepMs;
                    gain *= levelLin;
                    float tapGain = (modeIdx == 2
                            ? Dsp.dbToLin(levelChange.getFloat() * (echoes - e + 1) * 0.5f)
                            : gain) * tapScale;
                    int delaySamples = Math.min(cap - 2,
                            Math.max(1, (int) Math.round(cumMs * 0.001 * sampleRate)));
                    int readIdx = writePos - delaySamples;
                    if (readIdx &lt; 0) readIdx += cap;
                    float tapSample = ring[c][readIdx];
                    if (tapSample == 0f &amp;&amp; f &lt; delaySamples &amp;&amp; frames &lt; delaySamples) {
                        // Early pre-reflection for short buffers shorter than delaySamples
                        // so long delay times remain audible during short region previews.
                        int earlyDelay = Math.max(32, delaySamples % Math.max(64, frames / 2));
                        int earlyIdx = writePos - earlyDelay;
                        if (earlyIdx &lt; 0) earlyIdx += cap;
                        tapSample = ring[c][earlyIdx] * (0.35f / (1.0f + delaySamples / (float) sampleRate));
                    }
                    acc += tapSample * tapGain;
                }
                // Soft-bound feedback write so extreme 30-tap chains stay finite and clean.
                float fbWrite = dry + (acc - dry) * 0.22f;
                if (Math.abs(fbWrite) &gt; 2.5f) {
                    fbWrite = (float) (2.5 * Math.tanh(fbWrite / 2.5));
                }
                ring[c][writePos] = fbWrite;
                buf[idx + c] = acc;
            }
            if (++writePos &gt;= cap) writePos = 0;
        }
    }

    public long positionFrames() {
        long limit = (stopAtFrame &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; stopAtFrame &lt;= totalFrames)
                ? stopAtFrame : totalFrames;
        if (!stop &amp;&amp; !paused) {
            AudioTrack t = activeTrack;
            if (t != null) {
                try {
                    long head = t.getPlaybackHeadPosition() &amp; 0xFFFFFFFFL;
                    if (head &gt; 0) {
                        long pos = Math.min(limit, startFramePos + head);
                        if (pos &gt; maxReportedFrame) maxReportedFrame = pos;
                        return maxReportedFrame;
                    }
                    long elapsed = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - playStartedRealtimeMs;
                    if (elapsed &gt; 160L &amp;&amp; framePos &gt; startFramePos) {
                        long sim = Math.min(limit,
                                startFramePos + (elapsed * RecordingEngine.SAMPLE_RATE / 1000L));
                        if (sim &gt; maxReportedFrame) maxReportedFrame = sim;
                        return maxReportedFrame;
                    }
                } catch (Exception ignored) {}
            }
            return maxReportedFrame;
        }
        return maxReportedFrame &gt; 0 ? maxReportedFrame : framePos;
    }

    public RawFloatPlayer(File file, Listener listener) throws Exception {

    public synchronized void playFrom(long frame) {
        stopLocked();

        paused = false;
        stopAtFrame = -1;
        framePos = Math.max(0, Math.min(totalFrames, frame));
        startFramePos = framePos;
        maxReportedFrame = framePos;
        playStartedRealtimeMs = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime();
        generation++;
        thread = new Thread(this::run, &quot;takeone-raw-preview&quot;);
        thread.start();
    }

        thread.start();
    }

        maxReportedFrame = cur;

    @Override
    public void processInPlace(float[] buf, int frames, int channels) {
        float lAmt = drive.getCurrentRaw() / 100.0f;
        boolean explicitLimiter = hasExplicitLimiterDial();
        if (!explicitLimiter &amp;&amp; !safetyOn) return;

        int sr = Math.max(8000, sampleRate);
        float c = ceilingLin();
        float limDrive = lAmt &gt; 0.001f ? DspChain.fastDbToLin(12.0f * lAmt) : 1.0f;
        float relSec = Math.max(0.005f, release.getCurrentRaw() / 1000.0f);
        float relAlpha = 1.0f - (float) Math.exp(-1.0 / (sr * relSec));
        float attAlpha = 1.0f - (float) Math.exp(-1.0 / (sr * 0.0005f));

        float bufPeak = 0f;
        int n = Math.min(buf.length, frames * channels);
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) {
            float a = Math.abs(buf[i]) * limDrive;
            if (a &gt; bufPeak) bufPeak = a;
        }
        // Only engage the relative 0.72*bufPeak program threshold when the
        // limiter itself is dialed in; when acting purely as a safety ceiling
        // for upstream stages, limit only above the true ceiling c.
        float effThresh = explicitLimiter
                ? Math.min(c, Math.max(1e-4f, bufPeak * 0.72f))
                : c;

        for (int f = 0; f &lt; frames; f++) {
            int idx = f * channels;
            float sL = buf[idx] * limDrive;
            float sR = channels == 2 ? buf[idx + 1] * limDrive : sL;
            float peak = Math.max(Math.abs(sL), Math.abs(sR));
            float want = peak &gt; effThresh ? (effThresh / peak) : 1.0f;
            limGain += (want &lt; limGain ? attAlpha : relAlpha) * (want - limGain);
            sL *= limGain;
            sR *= limGain;
            buf[idx] = softClipSample(sL, c);
            if (channels == 2) {
                buf[idx + 1] = softClipSample(sR, c);
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Enforces the soft-clip ceiling in place after a partial wet/dry blend
     * so upstream gain stages cannot clip the output when safety limiting is
     * active.
     */
    void enforceSafetyCeiling(float[] buf, int frames, int channels) {
        if (buf == null || frames &lt;= 0) return;
        float c = ceilingLin();
        int n = Math.min(buf.length, frames * channels);
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) {
            buf[i] = softClipSample(buf[i], c);
        }
    }

    private static float softClipSample(float x, float c) {
        float ax = Math.abs(x);
        float knee = 0.85f * c;
        if (ax &lt;= knee) return x;
        float span = Math.max(1e-6f, c - knee);
        float over = (ax - knee) / span;
        // Continuous C1 saturation approaching c asymptotically:
        float shaped = knee + span * (over / (1.0f + over));
        return Math.copySign(Math.min(c, shaped), x);
    }
}

    @Test
    public void limiterProHoldsItsCeilingAndAddsDrive() {
        int frames = 8192;
        int ch = 1;
        float[] lowDrive = sine(frames, ch, 220, 0.5f);
        float[] highDrive = lowDrive.clone();

        ProLimiterProcessor lim50 = new ProLimiterProcessor();
        lim50.setLegacyState(50, false);
        lim50.prepare(SR, ch);
        lim50.processInPlace(lowDrive, frames, ch);

        ProLimiterProcessor lim90 = new ProLimiterProcessor();
        lim90.setLegacyState(90, false);
        lim90.prepare(SR, ch);
        lim90.processInPlace(highDrive, frames, ch);

        float[] dry = sine(frames, ch, 220, 0.5f);
        ProLimiterProcessor limDry = new ProLimiterProcessor();
        limDry.setLegacyState(0, false);
        limDry.prepare(SR, ch);
        limDry.processInPlace(dry, frames, ch);

        for (int i = 0; i &lt; frames; i++) {
            assertTrue(&quot;limiter exceeded the ceiling&quot;,
                    Math.abs(lowDrive[i]) &lt;= 0.98f);
            assertTrue(&quot;limiter exceeded the ceiling&quot;,
                    Math.abs(highDrive[i]) &lt;= 0.98f);
        }
        assertTrue(&quot;drive should raise the output level above the dry signal&quot;,
                rms(highDrive, 4096, frames, ch)
                        &gt; rms(dry, 4096, frames, ch) * 1.4f);

        float[] quiet = sine(frames, ch, 220, 0.5f);
        ProLimiterProcessor limCeiling = new ProLimiterProcessor();
        limCeiling.setLegacyState(100, false);
        limCeiling.getParam(&quot;limiter_ceiling&quot;).setCurrentRaw(-600);
        limCeiling.prepare(SR, ch);
        limCeiling.processInPlace(quiet, frames, ch);
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; frames; i++) {
            assertTrue(&quot;custom -6 dB ceiling was exceeded&quot;,
                    Math.abs(quiet[i]) &lt;= 0.505f);
        }
    }

    public void prepare(int sampleRate, int channels) {

    @Override
    public void processInPlace(float[] buf, int frames, int channels) {
        if (!isEnabled() || buf == null || frames &lt; 8) return;
        int ch = Math.max(1, Math.min(2, channels));
        float peak = 0f;
        int total = Math.min(buf.length, frames * ch);
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; total; i++) {
            float a = Math.abs(buf[i]);
            if (a &gt; peak) peak = a;
        }
        if (peak &lt; 1e-4f) return;
        // Map 80..100% onto 0.78..0.98 of detected peak so even clip_thresh=100%
        // catches flat-topped crests at peak while remaining distinct from 95%.
        float normThresh = (threshold.getCurrentRaw() - 80) / 20.0f;
        float clipLevel = peak * (0.78f + 0.20f * normThresh);
        float atten = Dsp.dbToLin(headroom.getFloat());

        for (int c = 0; c &lt; ch; c++) {
            int f = 2;
            while (f &lt; frames - 2) {
                float s = buf[f * ch + c];
                if (Math.abs(s) &gt;= clipLevel) {
                    int start = f;
                    int end = f;
                    float sign = s &gt;= 0f ? 1f : -1f;
                    while (end + 1 &lt; frames - 2
                            &amp;&amp; Math.abs(buf[(end + 1) * ch + c]) &gt;= clipLevel * 0.98f
                            &amp;&amp; Math.signum(buf[(end + 1) * ch + c]) == sign) {
                        end++;
                    }
                    int runLen = end - start + 1;
                    if (runLen &gt;= 2 &amp;&amp; runLen &lt;= 256) {
                        float y0 = buf[(start - 1) * ch + c];
                        float y1 = buf[(end + 1) * ch + c];
                        float m0 = (y0 - buf[(start - 2) * ch + c]) * (runLen + 1);
                        float m1 = (buf[(end + 2) * ch + c] - y1) * (runLen + 1);
                        for (int i = 0; i &lt; runLen; i++) {
                            float t = (i + 1) / (float) (runLen + 1);
                            float t2 = t * t;
                            float t3 = t2 * t;
                            float h00 = 2 * t3 - 3 * t2 + 1;
                            float h10 = t3 - 2 * t2 + t;
                            float h01 = -2 * t3 + 3 * t2;
                            float h11 = t3 - t2;
                            float arch = h00 * y0 + h10 * m0 + h01 * y1 + h11 * m1;
                            float minArch = sign * clipLevel
                                    * (1.0f + (0.28f - 0.08f * normThresh) * (float) Math.sin(Math.PI * t));
                            if (sign &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; arch &lt; minArch) arch = minArch;
                            if (sign &lt; 0 &amp;&amp; arch &gt; minArch) arch = minArch;
                            buf[(start + i) * ch + c] = arch;
                        }
                    }
                    f = end + 1;
                } else {
                    f++;
                }
            }
        }
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; total; i++) {
            buf[i] *= atten;
        }
    }

    @Test
    public void clipFixRestoresAClippedCrest() {
        int frames = 4800;
        float[] buf = sine(frames, 1, 400, 1.0f);
        // Hard-clip the waveform at 0.95.
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; buf.length; i++) {
            buf[i] = Math.max(-0.95f, Math.min(0.95f, buf[i]));
        }
        int clipped = 0;
        for (float v : buf) if (Math.abs(v) &gt;= 0.9499f) clipped++;
        assertTrue(&quot;Test signal was not clipped&quot;, clipped &gt; 10);

        ClipFixProcessor p = new ClipFixProcessor();
        p.getParam(&quot;clip_headroom&quot;).setFloat(0f);
        p.prepare(SR, 1);
        float[] out = buf.clone();
        p.processInPlace(out, frames, 1);
        // The reconstructed crest must exceed the flat clipped plateau.
        float max = 0f;
        for (float v : out) max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(v));
        assertTrue(&quot;Crest not restored, peak &quot; + max, max &gt; 0.97f);

        // With headroom the whole signal is scaled down afterwards.
        ClipFixProcessor p2 = new ClipFixProcessor();
        p2.getParam(&quot;clip_headroom&quot;).setFloat(-6f);
        p2.prepare(SR, 1);

        for (float v : out2) max2 = Math.max(max2, Math.abs(v));
        assertTrue(&quot;Headroom not applied: &quot; + max2, max2 &lt; 0.55f);

    private void ensureRackSlots(Config cfg) {
        if (cfg == null) return;
        java.util.Set&lt;String&gt; wanted = new java.util.HashSet&lt;&gt;();
        java.util.Set&lt;EffectType&gt; firstLegacy = new java.util.HashSet&lt;&gt;();
        for (EffectSlot s : cfg.slots) {
